# Runs from the editor

The [editor extensions](./editors) run your tests where you edit them, then show a run's progress in the status bar
and its results over the latest CI run's [failures](./editor-failures).

## Run tests

- The lines above a locator line, an application file or a page file (CodeLens in VS Code, Code Vision in a JetBrains
  IDE) run the tests they name when clicked; those of a server file record its
  [coverage](./editor-coverage#refresh-the-marks-with-a-local-run).
- **Piwi: Run the test at the cursor** (`Ctrl+Shift+Alt+K`, `Cmd+Shift+Alt+K` on macOS, another [key](/reference/editor-commands#keys) in some JetBrains keymaps) runs the test whose `test(…)`
  call holds the cursor, and **Piwi: Run this spec** every test of the spec; both in the editor's **Piwi** submenu
  on a spec and under VS Code's editor title Run button (the caret in a JetBrains IDE), saving the spec first. **Run** in VS Code's test hover runs it, as
  [the Testing view](#the-testing-view-vs-code) does. A test the instance does not know, such as one just
  [recorded](./editor-recording#run-it-or-verify-it-three-times), runs by its `test(…)` call's line,
  with or without an instance.
- **Piwi: Debug the test at the cursor** (**Debug the test at the caret**) runs it as **Debug with Piwi** does:
  headed, at [your breakpoints](./editor-breakpoints), holding each failure at its line.
- **Piwi: Verify the test at the cursor ×3** (**Verify the test at the caret ×3**) runs it three times as a
  [verification](#when-your-run-ends).
- **Piwi: Run the tests that reach this file** runs every test reaching the active file through
  [code reach](/features/code-reach); also in the editor's and file tree's **Piwi** submenu.
- **Piwi: Run a saved selection…** runs a [selection](/features/test-selection).

The command, `npx playwright test` with `piwi run`'s arguments, runs from the Playwright config's folder: as a task
in VS Code, in a terminal of its own (**Tasks: Rerun Last Task** restarts it), in the Run tool window in a JetBrains
IDE, its tests in a test tree beside the output as they run (**Rerun** restarts it), or in the IDE's Playwright runner
(Debug, **Rerun Failed Tests**), a choice of **Settings → Tools → Piwi**, offered once, that keeps every control of a
Piwi run, through the runner's Rerun and Debug too. It sets `PIWI_ORIGIN=editor` and its own `PIWI_ORIGIN_REF`
([run origin](/reference/test-metadata#run-origin)), by which the editor finds its run. Breakpoints and the editor pause it:
[Pause and step from the editor](./editor-run-control).

## How a run starts

Two choices apply to every run: **Run headed** (`--headed`, a verification included) and
[**Hold failures**](./watch-a-run#hold-failures) **Auto**, **On** or **Off** from the run's start. Auto lets Piwi
decide: on with your breakpoints or a `page.pause()`, headed for the latter.
**Piwi: Turn headed runs on or off** and **Piwi: Hold failures from each run's start…** set them (in VS Code,
`piwi.runHeaded` and `piwi.runHoldFailures`, shown in the status bar's tooltip and offered together by **Piwi: Run
options…**). A
[debug run](./debug-in-editor), a Flake Lab line and a fix plan's check leave them out.

## The Testing view (VS Code)

VS Code's Testing view lists the tests `playwright test --list --project=*` gives for each config, under their folders
and `test.describe` blocks, a test of several Playwright projects with a node per project, each with its latest result
and duration, and where and why it failed (**Peek Error**). A spec is listed again when saved, and read from its text
while you edit it. A config Playwright cannot list says why. Tests only your instance knows go in
**Not in this checkout**, which does not run. Results are published as a test run (`Piwi: run #120 on main`); a run in progress shows each test as
it begins and ends. Its gutter shows each result in place of Piwi's icon; the line keeps Piwi's hover. A flaky test
shows as passed, its line ending with _flaky_. An item is named by its test's title alone, as a screen reader reads it,
and the view's filter finds tests by `@piwi:flaky`, `@piwi:quarantined`, a Playwright tag (`@piwi:@smoke`) or an owner
(`@piwi:owner:ada`). With the view off, Piwi's gutter marks a test with no recent result with a dashed ring.

Each test's actions are one list in both editors: **Run with Piwi**, **Debug with Piwi** and **Verify ×3 with Piwi**,
**Record steps in this test…** (a [recording](./editor-recording) after the last line of its body), a failure's trace
and screenshot, **Open in dashboard**, **Copy context for agent**, then the test's Flake Lab commands. **More…** on the [test's card](./editor-test-card) opens them, and in VS Code **Piwi: Show the test's actions…**
from the Testing view's gutter and menus, and the line number's menu with the view off; in a JetBrains IDE, a
right-click on the result icon. The IDE's own run
icon offers **Run with Piwi** and **Verify ×3 with Piwi** too; turning off **Piwi test results** under **Gutter Icons**
hides the result icon and its list.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/vscode-testing.png" alt="VS Code: the Testing view lists the spec's tests with their latest results, and a failing test's error is peeked at its line in the spec">
  <figcaption>The Testing view with the latest run's results, and why <strong>pays by card</strong> failed, at its line.</figcaption>
</figure>

**Run with Piwi**, the view's run profile, runs what you pick by the narrowest filter Playwright takes: a config whole, a
folder or a spec by its path, a describe block or a test by its line (a loop's by its title), a project's node, and a
test Playwright runs only when named (`default: false`), with `--project`. **Debug with Piwi** runs them headed at your breakpoints,
holding each failure, and **Verify ×3 with Piwi** three times. Under Run with Coverage, it also shows their
coverage in the Test Coverage view ([Editor coverage](./editor-coverage)). From a failed test's actions, **Debug with Piwi** runs it as [Debug in my
editor](./debug-in-editor) does, stopping once at the line it failed through. A test the run gave Piwi no result for
passes when the command exited with 0, else is an error. Debug runs Piwi's run control, not a debug session.
`piwi.testExplorer` turns the view's Piwi tests off.

## Re-run the failing tests

**Piwi: Re-run the failing tests** (`Ctrl+Shift+Alt+F`, `Cmd+Shift+Alt+F` on macOS, as [Keys](/reference/editor-commands#keys) lists; **Tools → Piwi → Re-run the
failing tests**) runs every test still failing, or edited since its run, one command per Playwright config, or those
of one config from its node in the [failures view](./editor-failures#the-failures-view); when none fails, it says so.

## After a run

Within a second of a run of the project ending, the editor reads the branch's latest run and its failures again,
told by the instance's event stream; else every five minutes with the stream, every minute without. A checkout
or a commit is noticed within seconds: the editor reads that run again and compares your application
files with the new `HEAD`.

A run started from the editor is its own wherever it runs: the status bar follows it, the gutter shows each test as
running, then its result, and its failures read _your run #124_ once it ends. The editor learns the command's end and
exit code from the process it started, in every shell, a rerun included. When no run on the instance carries its ref,
it says why: its reporter sent nothing (its lines in the output name the server address, the key, or a refusal), or
the config has no Piwi reporter: `The run ended (exit code 1) but did not
reach https://piwi.example.com: is the Piwi reporter in the Playwright config?`

## When your run ends

Once a run you started from the editor, [a terminal](./terminal-runs) (`run #125 in a terminal`) or the IDE's test
runner is read, a notification says what it changed:
`Piwi: run #124 · 1 of 3 CI failures fixed, 2 still failing (login.spec.ts › logs in, checkout.spec.ts › pays)` and new
failures, with **Open the failures**, **Open in dashboard** and **Re-run failing**. The `piwi.runNotifications` setting
(**Settings → Tools → Piwi** in JetBrains) shows it when a test fails, the default, always (a passing run then offers
**Only on failure**), or never; **Settings** opens it in VS Code.

A CI run of your branch says the same once it ends, against the run it replaced:
`Piwi: CI run #130 on feature-x · 2 fixed · 1 new failure (cart.spec.ts › adds)`. The `piwi.runNotificationsScope`
setting, **The runs it says it for** in JetBrains, keeps it to the runs you started.

A [verification](/guide/concepts#verification), **Verify ×3**, runs the test three times without retries or
breakpoints (`--repeat-each=3 --retries=0`), each run a result on the instance, and holds no failure. Its notification
says how many passed, whatever the setting: `Piwi: run #124 · Passed 3 of 3`, or `Failed 1 of 3` with **Open the
failures** and **Open in dashboard**, counted from the results the run streams (`Failed at least 1 of 3` when some
were missed), else [from its exit code](./editor-recording#run-it-or-verify-it-three-times). Like a fix plan's verification and a
Flake Lab line, it is listed, paused and stopped as any run.

- [The editor's status bar](./editor-status-bar): the latest run, the run in progress, and when the item turns red.
- [Failures in the editor](./editor-failures): the failures a run leaves, at their lines and in the failures view.
- [Editor connection](./editor-connection): the instance the editor reads, and its key.

# Test card

A test's card answers "my bug or a flake?" without leaving the editor. In VS Code it is the test's hover on its
`test(…)` line; in a JetBrains IDE, a click on the test's result icon opens it.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/vscode-test-card.png" alt="VS Code: the hover on a failing test's line, its card: the latest runs as colored bars, how many passed and the median duration, the run it last failed in and why, then Run, Open in dashboard and More…">
  <figcaption>VS Code: the card in the hover on the test's line.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/jetbrains-test-card.png" alt="WebStorm: the card a click on a failing test's result icon opens: the test's title, its latest runs as colored bars and how they went, the run it last failed in and why, then Run, Open in dashboard and More…">
  <figcaption>A JetBrains IDE: the card a click on the test's result icon opens.</figcaption>
</figure>

## What it shows

- **The strip**: the test's latest runs, oldest on the left, one bar each in the dashboard's color for its outcome:
  green passed, red failed, fuchsia flaky (it passed on a retry), gray skipped. A run is one bar, whatever its retries,
  repetitions and projects: failed when one of them ended failed, flaky when one passed on a retry. Each bar links to
  its run, and its tooltip names the run, the outcome and how long the test took.
- **How far back**: twenty runs at most, read from the test's last 50 attempts, so a test run in three projects shows
  about sixteen, and one run with `--repeat-each` fewer still. The dashboard's test page holds its whole history.
- **How they went**: `Passed 17 of the last 20 runs · 2 flaky · median 1.4 s`, skipped runs left out.
- **The last failure**: the run it failed in, how long ago, and why in one line, in the editor's error color: the
  headline of its error (`Expected true, got false — toBe`).
- **Its owner, tags and quarantine**: the owner its `piwi:owner` annotation names, its Playwright tags, and, while it
  is [quarantined](./flaky-tests#quarantine-with-a-way-out), for how long and how many passes it has toward release.

Under the card, **Run** runs the test, **Open in dashboard** opens its page, and **More…** opens the test's actions:
[Runs from the editor](./editor-runs) lists them.

## Where it comes from

The editor reads the test's history from the instance as the card opens, and keeps it for 30 seconds. It waits for it
one and a half seconds at most: past that, the hover shows the test's result in one line, and a click in a JetBrains
IDE opens the test's actions. A test the instance does not know yet has no card.

## Related

- [Runs from the editor](./editor-runs)
- [Flaky tests](./flaky-tests)

<!-- https://piwitests.dev/features/editor-status-bar -->

# The editor's status bar

The Piwi item in the status bar of the [editor extensions](./editors) says how the latest run of your branch went, or
how far a run in progress is, for the Playwright config of the file you are editing, with its tests that may be
[stuck](./stuck-tests) (`· 1 stuck?`).

The latest complete run on the branch: how many tests passed, how many still fail (`Piwi: 2 failing`), or, with none
failing, how many your local runs fixed (`Piwi: 1 fixed locally`); its tooltip counts what your local runs fixed and the
flaky tests. A recording in progress takes the item, in both editors, its controls in the item's menu; a test that
waits for you keeps it. While a run started from this editor, or [another run of the branch](./editor-ci-runs),
is in progress, the item says where its test stands stopped or the call a paused one waits in, that it is shared live,
and how far it is (`Piwi: held at its failure · checkout.page.ts:12 · run #124 · 4 of 9 · 1 failed`), another's
naming its branch (`CI run #130 on feature-x`) and, in the tooltip, where it comes from (`from the desktop app`, `on a
developer's machine`), in the same words in both editors, and returns to the latest run when it ends. A test that waits for you marks the item until you
answer it: its background turns yellow in VS Code, and its icon takes a dot in a JetBrains IDE. A run you started keeps the item whichever Playwright config the active file belongs to, and VS Code's Testing
view shows a run that is not yours with its tests' results as they end, never as your tests running. The editor follows
the two newest CI runs of the branch, through the connection to the instance it already holds, and while it follows
one, the run's reporter streams the call each test is at.

With several Playwright configs, the item speaks for the config of the file you are editing, the deepest config folder
that holds it, and follows you from file to file; outside every config folder, it shows the first connected config.
Its tooltip names the config (`The active file's Playwright config, in apps/admin (one of 3)`), then holds the run's
counts, the baseline, your local runs since, the run in progress, and when the run was read (`Updated 12 s ago · live`
while the event stream is connected, `· read every minute` without it).

In VS Code, a click opens **Piwi: Open the Piwi menu**, in the JetBrains menu's sections, the item's own action first:
Enter reads the latest run and its failures again (**Refresh the latest run**), without the indexes and configs **Read
the instance and the configs again** reads, or goes to the stopped line while a test is stopped. The run's controls and
its share are in the menu while a run is live. When the extension is not connected, the item says why, and its first
entry is **Connect…**, or **Read the instance and the configs again** for an [unreachable
instance](./editor-connection#an-unreachable-instance) or a desktop app to restart.

The item turns red (its background in VS Code, its text in a JetBrains IDE) only for a test a run you started from
the editor failed that the baseline does not fail, until a run fixes it or the editor restarts: a CI failure or a
teammate's is counted, never red, and so is a run in progress. `piwi.statusBarAlert` in VS Code, and **The status bar item's text turns red** on
Settings → Tools → Piwi in a JetBrains IDE, choose any failing test or never instead.

In a JetBrains IDE, an icon before the text shows the state of the run the item counts (running, failing, passed), of a
recording, or of the connection. A click opens a menu of the **Tools → Piwi** actions that apply, led by what the item
calls for: **Refresh the latest run**, **Read the instance and the configs again** for an unreachable instance or a
desktop app to restart, **Connect…** while not connected, **Node.js settings…** when Node.js is missing or too old, or
**Go to the recorded lines** while a recording runs, with **Pause recording**, **Resume recording** and **Stop
recording**.

## Compare with another run

By default, failures are read against the checked-out branch's latest complete run, else the default branch's. **Piwi:
Compare with…** (**Tools → Piwi → Compare with…** in a JetBrains IDE, and the failures view's title bar) chooses another
run to compare with: a branch's latest complete run, a run by its id, or **My local runs only**, your runs from this
machine, without CI. Your runs since are laid over each. The status bar tooltip and the
failures view name it (`Baseline: CI run #120 on feature/x`), ending with `(no run)` when it found none. That run need
not have passed: it is not the dashboard's [baseline](/guide/concepts#baseline-last-green-run), the last passing run.
The choice is kept on this machine, per Playwright config.

## A test that waits for you

A test held at its failure, or stopped at `page.pause()`, while the editor is in the background, calls you once: a
notification with **Resume** and **Go to the stopped line** in VS Code, the system's attention request (a bouncing or
flashing icon) in a JetBrains IDE, which also comes to the front while you are in another application and the
debugger's **Focus application on breakpoint** is on, as it is by default. A stop you asked for, at a breakpoint, a **Step** or a **Pause**, never does, nor
one an agent drives or a desktop app's job, which calls from its own window.
[A paused run](./editor-run-control) has the controls, and [Runs from the editor](./editor-runs) starts them.

## Related

- [Runs from the editor](./editor-runs): run tests from the editor and see their results.
- [Failures in the editor](./editor-failures): the failures a run leaves, at their lines and in the failures view.
- [Editor connection](./editor-connection): the instance the editor reads, and its key.

# Runs started outside Piwi

A run you start yourself follows the VS Code or JetBrains window whose workspace holds it: `npx playwright test` in a
terminal, with a reporter and an editor extension newer than 0.62.0, or a JetBrains IDE's own Playwright run (the
gutter's **Run** and **Debug**, a Playwright run configuration), with a reporter newer than 0.63.0. It stops at the
editor's breakpoints, shows in the editor and in Piwi Picker's [Runs window](./runs-window), marked **Terminal** or
**Test runner**, and takes the same controls ([Pause and step from the editor](./editor-run-control)) but **Stop**: its
process is the terminal's or the IDE's. It says so as it starts:

```text
[Piwi Dashboard] Following this run in Visual Studio Code (pid 41230), whose breakpoints stop it: PIWI_EDITOR=off runs it alone.
```

With no editor window on its folder, a run in a folder [the desktop app](./desktop) links follows the app (a reporter
newer than 0.68.0): its Local runs tray lists it, pauses it and watches its workers, as it does
[the runs it starts](./desktop-runs), and Piwi Picker's Runs window holds its failures as you ask.

It runs as its config says, headless by default, so the editor shows a stop as
[a headless run's](./editor-run-control#a-headless-run): an image of its page, which the editor's paused page and Piwi
Picker's Runs window can watch live. To see the browser, add `--headed` to the command, or to the Playwright options
of the run configuration.

## Which editor, or the desktop app

Each editor window's Piwi service writes a file in `~/.piwi/editors` (`PIWI_EDITORS_DIR` names another folder) with
its workspace folders and where its runs connect. The run follows the window one of whose folders holds its Playwright
config's folder or its working directory, links resolved: the most specific folder wins, then the window that started
last. A window of another machine, another user's, or one whose process ended is never followed, nor is a file
written before the machine last started, any file of a folder another user can open, or (but on Windows) a window
whose runs would connect through a folder another user can open.

No window holding it, the run follows the desktop app whose linked folder holds it: the app names where its runs
connect in `~/.piwi/desktop.json` (`PIWI_DESKTOP_CONFIG` names another file) once its server is up, by the same rules.

## When it follows one

- **A run whose output goes to a terminal, or that a test runner started** (one that names its reporter's file in
  `PW_TEST_REPORTER`, as a JetBrains IDE's Playwright runner does), is attended: it stops at the breakpoints.
- **A run whose output goes to a file or a pipe**, as an agent's, follows unattended: it is listed and **Pause** stops
  it, but no breakpoint does and no failure waits. `PIWI_EDITOR=on` attends it. It says so as it starts
  ([the terminal's lines](#the-terminal-s-lines)).
- **Never** under CI, with Playwright's own debugger (`--debug`, `PWDEBUG=1`) or UI mode, when the run names its own
  `PIWI_RUN_CHANNEL`, or when the desktop app or another launcher started it.
- **`PIWI_EDITOR=off`** runs it alone.

## What it takes from the editor

- **The breakpoints**, with `piwi.breakpoints` set to **Every run** ([the setting](./editor-breakpoints#the-setting)):
  it starts with the editor's breakpoints as they are, then takes them as you change them. Otherwise, or without any,
  it runs as it would, and **Pause** stops it.
- **The controls**: Pause, Resume, Step, Run to the cursor, Finish and [End the test](./end-the-test), and the code a stop
  makes, Assert a region and Mock a request, written in the editor ([Code from a pause](./editor-stop-code)).
- **Record and Assert** in the test's window, through the editor's recorder, and **Pick a locator**, which goes
  to the editor (its Send to editor pairing), as for a run Piwi starts.
- **Its stops on the desktop app's page of the run**, for a run that reports to [the app](./desktop): which tests wait
  for the editor (**In Visual Studio Code**), each place opening in the IDE.
- **Failures.** A failure goes on, as without Piwi, until you turn the run's
  [**Hold failures**](./watch-a-run#hold-failures) on, in the editor or the Runs window.

When the editor closes, or its service stops, the connection closes, and a stop with no pause bar goes on. The token
of the editor's connection reaches the run's workers alone, out of the tests' environment while they run, as for a run
the editor starts.

## The terminal's lines

A run prints one line for its page, `[Piwi Dashboard] View live progress: …`, and one when it follows an editor or the
desktop app. A run whose output goes to a file or a pipe follows it unattended and says so:

```text
[Piwi Dashboard] Following this run in Visual Studio Code (pid 41230), unattended: its output goes to no terminal, so no failure waits and only a Pause stops it. PIWI_EDITOR=on attends it, PIWI_EDITOR=off runs it alone.
```

The other lines of a run's start (its project and Playwright version, its shard, the stream opening on time) are
printed with `PIWI_VERBOSE=true` alone. A stream that opens late, a failure link and a warning are always printed.

In a terminal outside CI, the run's page is a link. Windows Terminal and ConEmu show how far the run is in the tab and
the taskbar, and Ghostty 1.2 or later atop the terminal, red once a test failed. `PIWI_TERMINAL_PROGRESS=off` turns
both off, and `PIWI_TERMINAL_PROGRESS=on` sends the progress to any terminal: one that reads it as a notification
shows one at each step.

## A reproduction from the desktop app

A job the desktop app runs in a throwaway worktree of a commit follows your editor window as a terminal run does,
by the rules above: [A reproduction in your editor](./desktop-runs#a-reproduction-in-your-editor).

## Limits

- **Under the desktop app, a pick comes to its window to copy**, and Record and Assert, which need an editor, are
  not offered. An editor extension older than this one names no pairing for the run: start the test from the editor
  to pick there.
- **No Stop.** End the run in its terminal, or with the IDE's own **Stop**.
- **Debug stops twice.** Under a JetBrains IDE's **Debug**, a breakpoint stops the test in the debugger, then at Piwi's
  stop, whose controls take no key while the debug session runs. `PIWI_EDITOR=off` in the run configuration's
  environment leaves the breakpoints to the debugger.
- **Piwi's reporter in the config.** The run looks for an editor as the reporter starts (`wrapConfig` adds it): with
  the capture fixtures alone, it runs alone.
- **Your machine.** A run in a dev container or over SSH follows an editor whose service runs there too; the desktop
  app's folders are this machine's alone.

# Breakpoints in the browser

A breakpoint you set with the editor's own gutter click pauses the next test you debug with the [editor
extensions](./editors) (**Debug the test at the cursor**), in the browser, right before the call on its line that acts on, reads or checks the page: a navigation, a
click, a key press, an assertion. Piwi's bar at the top of the page lets you look at the page, step through the calls,
or pick a better locator, which lands back on that line in the editor. The stop is Playwright's own debugger
(`context.debugger`) without its Inspector: Piwi's bar answers it, and no JavaScript debugger attaches.

## Pause a run

1. Set a line breakpoint on a line with a Playwright call, in a spec, a page object or a fixture:
   `await page.getByText('Pay now').click();`, `await page.goto('/checkout');`, `await page.keyboard.press('Tab');`
   or `await expect(page).toHaveURL(/cart/);`. On a statement broken over lines, any of its lines will do.
2. Debug the test: **Debug with Piwi** in its actions, on its failure or in VS Code's Testing view. A plain Run stops
   only as [the setting](#the-setting) says.
3. The test stops before the call on your line runs. A run Piwi starts follows your config, headless unless it sets
   `headless: false` or you chose **Run headed** ([How a run starts](./editor-runs#how-a-run-starts)): the editor
   marks the line and shows the stopped page ([A headless run](./editor-run-control#a-headless-run)). In a headed run,
   the pause bar appears in the
   browser with the call as Playwright names it, `Paused at login.spec.ts:42 · Click getByText('Pay now')`, and a
   locator call's element is highlighted.

The pause bar's buttons:

| Button                      | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Resume** (<kbd>Esc</kbd>) | Runs on to the next breakpoint                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Step**                    | Pauses again before the next call that acts on, reads or checks the page, breakpoint or not                                                                                                                     |
| **Pick a locator**          | Opens Piwi's [element picker](/features/locator-healing#pick-a-replacement-locator-on-the-failing-page-local-runs): pick the element, choose stable parents, confirm a ranked locator; the bar comes back after |
| **Record**                  | Records what you do in the page into the editor, above the paused line: [Record from a pause](#record-from-a-pause)                                                                                             |
| **Finish**                  | Runs on without pausing again in this test                                                                                                                                                                      |
| **End the test**            | [Skips the rest of the test](./end-the-test)                                                                                                                                                                    |

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/picker-pause.png" alt="A shop page in the browser, paused before a click on Checkout: the button highlighted, Piwi's pause bar at the top with Resume, Step, Pick a locator, Record and Finish">
  <figcaption>A run paused before the click on <strong>Checkout</strong>: the element highlighted, and Piwi's bar at the top of the page.</figcaption>
</figure>

The page under the bar stays live: scroll it, open the browser's developer tools, or click through it before you
resume. The test timeout stops while the test is paused; [Time paused at a stop](./slow-tests#time-paused-at-a-stop) says which waits keep their
deadline, and how the dashboard counts the time paused.

## Where the pick lands

A locator you confirm replaces the locator chain on the breakpoint's line, in the file as it stands, saved or not:
`page.getByText('Pay now').click()` becomes `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay now' }).click()`, and a
notification says so. When the line holds no locator, because you edited it during the pause or it takes its locator
from a page object (`checkout.payButton().click()`), the locator is inserted at the cursor instead, and the
notification says why.

The pick is also printed in the run's terminal (`[piwi] Locator picked at tests/login.spec.ts:42: getByRole(…)`) and
recorded in the run's locator snapshots, so the [Locator fix](/features/locator-healing) panel shows it as **Your
pick** once the run uploads.

The pick reaches the editor through the address [Piwi Picker sends to](./editor-recording#send-from-piwi-picker);
nothing is copied to the clipboard.

## Record from a pause

**Record** hands the paused page to the editor's [recorder](./editor-recording): the steps you take from there
are written into the file on a new line above the paused statement (the first line of a statement broken over lines),
on the page expression in scope there, as **Record here** in the editor writes them, but with no `page.goto`: the page
is where the test left it, signed in and filled in as the test made it. The editor opens the file at that line and
starts recording. Pause and Stop are in the recorder's bar in the page and in the editor; once you stop, the pause bar
comes back, and **Resume** runs the rest of the test from the page as you left it, which checks that the new steps fit
what follows.

`await page.pause()` in a test does the same without a breakpoint: in a run Piwi starts or
[that follows your editor](./terminal-runs), or any headed run with breakpoints, it stops there under Piwi's pause bar
in place of Playwright's Inspector (headless, in the editor), with **Record** among its
buttons in a run Piwi starts or that follows your editor, and Piwi adds `--headed` to a run whose spec holds a `page.pause()` call. The
`page.pause()` line stays, so the next run can record from there again; remove it when the test is done. In any other
run, outside a test (a `beforeAll` or `afterAll`) and on a page of a browser the
test launched itself, `page.pause()` is Playwright's own, with its Inspector; in a headless browser it returns at
once.
**Record** records http(s) pages: on a page the test made with `setContent`, or a `file:` page, the editor says
so and nothing is recorded.

The test reaches the editor through `PIWI_RECORD_CHANNEL`, the socket of
[the run's connection](./editor-run-control#how-it-works); a recording not started within 30 seconds is refused, and
the test goes on.

## The setting

`piwi.breakpoints` (VS Code), or **The runs that pause at the editor's breakpoints** (**Settings → Tools → Piwi**),
says which runs stop: **Debug with Piwi** (the default), **Every run** (terminal runs too), or **Never**.

## What it needs

- **`@piwitests/reporter` 0.48.0 or later**, with the [capture fixtures](/guide/capture-fixtures) in your tests: the
  pause runs in them. With an older one, the run starts anyway and the editor warns once. A reporter of 0.59.0 or
  older pauses before locator actions and assertions only. A spec that imports `test` from `@playwright/test` never
  stops, and the run's output names it once.
- **A run started from Piwi**, or [started outside Piwi](./terminal-runs). The editor passes the breakpoints under the
  Playwright config's folder to the run as `PIWI_PAUSE_AT` (`tests/login.spec.ts:42;tests/pages/checkout.page.ts:9`,
  relative to that folder), with its pairing address as `PIWI_EDITOR_SEND`. It adds `--headed` when you chose
  **Run headed**, or when the reporter stops only headed: older than 0.62.0, of an unknown version, or with no run
  channel to show a headless stop. Set `PIWI_PAUSE_AT` yourself to
  [pause a run you start](/features/locator-healing#pause-at-a-breakpoint-local-runs).

## Limits

- **The bar needs a headed browser, and a local run.** Under CI (a provider's variable such as `GITHUB_ACTIONS`, or `CI` not `false` or `0`) or
  Playwright's debugger (`--debug`, `PWDEBUG`), the run ignores breakpoints, saying why once, as does a headless
  run of yours with `PIWI_PAUSE_AT`; one Piwi starts stops with no bar, and the editor shows its page
  ([A headless run](./editor-run-control#a-headless-run)).
- **Only the calls Playwright's debugger stops at pause**: navigations, actions, key presses and mouse moves,
  assertions, `evaluate`, `waitForFunction`, screenshots and an element's reads (`textContent`, `inputValue`,
  `getAttribute`, `isVisible`, `count`). `waitForTimeout`, `waitForSelector`, `waitForURL`, `waitForEvent`, `title()`
  and `ariaSnapshot()` never do, so a breakpoint on such a line, on a helper call or on a line with no Playwright call
  does nothing. A breakpoint in a page object method pauses every test that calls it.
- **A run with breakpoints stops before every call** and lets those off your lines go on at once, at about a millisecond
  a call.
- **The paused call lasts as long as you looked** at the page, in Playwright's trace, its HTML report and the
  dashboard's steps; only the statistics leave it out.
- **A call the test ended under runs** as the bar goes away, during teardown, when the test fails under the bar or does
  not await the call; the call is waited for, up to two seconds, so its requests stay the test's.
- **One Inspector switch per worker.** While Playwright's own `page.pause()` runs, a stop in another context opens its
  Inspector too, and a context that opened one keeps it. A `page.pause()` on a browser launched through a second copy
  of Playwright shows neither bar nor Inspector and waits until the test's timeout.
- **Every attempt pauses.** With retries, a test pauses again on its retry, and the bar says `attempt 2`.
- **Each worker pauses its own browser.** When several tests reach a breakpoint, run `--workers=1` to pause one at a
  time.
- **Record** is offered from Piwi's pause bar only, never from a debugger paused in your code.
- **Record** records the paused page alone: a tab or a popup it opens is not recorded, as in any recording.

# Pause and step from the editor

A test run the [editor extensions](./editors) start, or [one started outside Piwi](./terminal-runs), can be paused,
stepped and resumed from the editor with Piwi's own commands: no debug session starts, and the IDE's debugger works
as usual beside it. The editor marks the line the test stopped at, and the breakpoints you set or remove reach the run
while it goes on. The [pause bar](./editor-breakpoints#pause-a-run) and Piwi Picker's [Runs window](./runs-window)
answer the same stops; the code a stop writes is on [Code from a pause](./editor-stop-code).

## The controls

| Control | What it does | VS Code | JetBrains IDEs |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Pause** | Stops a running test before its next call that acts on, reads or checks the page | none | Pause Program's |
| **Resume** | Runs the stopped test on to the next breakpoint | `F5` | Resume Program's, `F9` |
| **Step** | Runs the call and stops before the next one, breakpoint or not | `F10` | Step Over's, `F8` |
| **Run to the cursor** | Stops at the first call on the cursor's line (on a statement broken over lines, at its call), or at a breakpoint before it | `Ctrl+F10` | Run to Cursor's, `Alt+F9` |
| **Finish** | Runs the test on without stopping at a breakpoint again in this attempt | `Shift+F11` | Step Out's, `Shift+F8` |
| **End the test** | [Skips the rest of the test](./end-the-test), and a stopped locator call from Playwright 1.62 | none | none |
| **Stop** | Ends the run's process | `Shift+F5` | **Stop the run**, or the Run tool window's Stop |

The keys are the IDE's debugger keys (in a JetBrains IDE, [your keymap's](./jetbrains)), Piwi's only while their control
applies and the debugger does not take them. On macOS, `Cmd+F10` runs to the cursor in VS Code. **Pause** and **End the
test** have no key in VS Code: bind one in **Preferences: Open Keyboard Shortcuts** (search `piwi`). Within two seconds
of an answer, until that worker stops, a key answers no other worker and starts no debug session.

Each editor puts them where its debugger keeps its own, and in the status item's menu, whose text says why and where
a test stopped: [Editor commands](/reference/editor-commands#where-the-run-controls-are) lists the places. From its
start, before a web server or a global setup lets Playwright report, the item says the run is starting, and **Stop**
ends it.

The item's line comes from the run, so it counts offline and with the desktop app
([Follow a run](./watch-a-run#how-far-it-is)); its tooltip names the other tools that have the run open.

**Pause** stops every run Piwi started in this window (a JetBrains IDE's project), each worker before its next
call that Playwright's debugger stops at ([which calls](./editor-breakpoints#limits)): a long call or a `waitForTimeout`
finishes first ([End the test](./end-the-test#while-a-pause-waits-for-a-call) gives up a locator call at once), and a
worker between tests stops at the next test's first call. A test that never stops, under CI or
Playwright's debugger, says why.

## Where the test stands

When a test stops, at a breakpoint, after **Step** or **Pause**, on the line it was run to, at `page.pause()`, or at
[a failure](./editor-stop-code#a-failure), the editor opens the file of the call about to run, with the cursor on its
line, and marks it:
an arrow in the gutter, the debugger's execution point color, and above it the call, as Playwright names it, with the
controls:

`Stopped at a breakpoint · Fill "MORNING10" getByLabel('Coupon code') · attempt 2`  Resume  Step  Finish  Write code…

It says [why the test stopped](./watch-a-run#where-a-test-stopped); `attempt 2` shows on a retry. Its test's gutter mark shows it paused. Both editors' line holds Resume, Step, Finish and **Write code…** (Resume alone at a failure), VS Code's lenses giving way; VS Code's hover holds all controls;
the color is `piwi.executionPointBackground`. In a JetBrains IDE the line is an inlay whose words are links,
the arrow's click and the inlay's context menu list the controls, and the color is **Settings → Editor → Color Scheme → Piwi → Line a run is
stopped at**. The mark goes when the test goes on (from the editor or the bar), ends, or closes its page.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/vscode-run-control-hover.png" alt="VS Code: a test paused at a page object's line, its hover naming the call that runs next with Resume, Step, Run to the cursor and Finish, and Resume, Step and Finish above the line">
  <figcaption>A run paused before it types the coupon.</figcaption>
</figure>

With several workers stopped, each has its own mark. A stop takes the cursor only on the worker you last answered or
worked on, or as the first shown while no step waits; another opens beside your editor, or, in a busy JetBrains IDE,
waits in the status bar's menu. The controls above a line act on its worker, a key or command on the one at the
cursor's line, else the only one shown, else it asks which. A control answers the stop it was shown for: when the test
went on meanwhile, it says so and asks nothing.

The run's code is your files as they stood when it started. The mark follows lines you add or remove above it, and
**Run to the cursor** in an edited file runs to the run's line for the cursor's, or says a line written since has none.

## A headless run

A run Piwi starts follows your config, headless by default, unless you turn
[headed runs](./editor-runs#how-a-run-starts) on or an [older reporter](./editor-breakpoints#what-it-needs) needs it. A headless stop opens its worker's page (`Piwi: worker 1` beside VS Code's editor, the JetBrains tool window's
**Worker 1** tab) with the line's controls, unless that worker's [watch](./watch-running-test) shows it. It keeps its
stop until it goes on, after a **Step** or **Run to the cursor** from the editor waits up to 10 seconds for the next,
and **Piwi: Show the paused page** (**Tools → Piwi → Run control**) opens it at any stop.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/vscode-run-control-paused-page.png" alt="VS Code: a headless test paused before it clicks Apply, and beside the editor the Piwi: worker 1 tab showing the cart page with the coupon typed in">
  <figcaption>A headless run paused before it clicks Apply: the page at the stop, beside the editor.</figcaption>
</figure>

Clicking the image picks a locator when the reporter supports it, on Playwright 1.60 or later: it replaces the
stopped line's, and the tab shows the result or refusal.

**Watch** updates the page until you hide or close the tab, resume or switch stops, and
[**Interact**](./watch-running-test#interact) plays your input on it, taking the stop.
It needs no Piwi Picker ([remote development](/guide/remote-development)), and older reporters keep the still image. To watch the test before it stops: [Watch a local test](./watch-running-test).

## Share with Playwright tools

At a stop, **Share with Playwright tools** (the stop's hover and **Piwi: Share the stopped test's browser with
Playwright tools** in VS Code; the stop's menu and **Tools → Piwi → Run control** in a JetBrains IDE) binds the test's browser for
Playwright's own tools, so `npx playwright cli attach piwi-<run>-w<worker>` and Playwright's dashboard can join it.
It is off until you ask, and asks first each time: any process of yours can then read the browser's pages and run code
in them. It stays shared until the test ends; no agent can share it.

## Breakpoints while the run goes on

A breakpoint you add, remove or toggle applies to the run from its next call, in every worker, later ones included.
One that only moves because you edited the lines above it keeps the line the run has, and one you set in an edited file
applies to that line of the run's code. The breakpoints that count are those a run's start reads: line
breakpoints in script files under a Playwright config's folder, in a Debug with Piwi run ([the
setting](./editor-breakpoints#the-setting) widens this). A logpoint, or a breakpoint that does not suspend, never stops
the test; a condition is not read, so a conditional breakpoint stops at each pass.

## How it works

<figure>
  <img src="/diagrams/run-control.svg" alt="A test run's workers report to the editor service through the run channel, which the IDE and Piwi Picker (over a WebSocket) steer; the pause bar shows in the test's browser only at a stop">
</figure>

With a reporter newer than 0.59.0, each worker of a Piwi run stays connected to the editor service through a socket
only you can read (`PIWI_RUN_CHANNEL`), saying which test it runs and where it stops. Closing the IDE closes the connections: a stop with no pause bar then goes on, one the bar shows waits there.

## Limits

- **No mark on a breakpoint that never stops.** One on a line with no call Playwright's debugger stops at looks like
  any other and does nothing.
- **Playwright calls, not JavaScript.** **Step** goes from one Playwright call to the next; stepping through the
  test's code stays with the IDE's debugger.
- **No image when the page is unknown.** A stop at a call other than a locator's (a navigation, a key press) in a
  browser context with several pages has no image, and refuses Piwi Picker's **Pick** and **Record**: the worker
  cannot tell its page. Any page of that context closing ends it.

- [Runs from the editor](./editor-runs): the commands that start a run.
- [Share a local run live](./share-live): for a teammate.
- [Debug in my editor](./debug-in-editor): a run started from a failure's page.
- [Remote development](/guide/remote-development): remote windows and JetBrains Gateway.

# Code from a pause

When a test stops in a run the [editor extensions](./editors) started, or [one that follows them](./terminal-runs), at a breakpoint, after **Pause** or **Step**,
or at a failure, the editor offers code written from the page as it stands: an assertion of what you see, a mock of a
request the page made, a better locator, the missing steps. The work on the page happens in the test's own browser;
the editor service writes the code, and the editor puts it above the stopped line. The controls that move the test
are on [Pause and step from the editor](./editor-run-control).

## The actions

| Action | What is written | Where it runs |
|---|---|---|
| **Pick a locator** | The locator of the element you pick, in place of the locator chain on the stopped line | The test's window, as the pause bar's [Pick a locator](./editor-breakpoints#where-the-pick-lands) |
| **Record** | The steps you take, above the stopped line | The test's window, as the bar's [Record](./editor-breakpoints#record-from-a-pause) |
| **Assert** | The check you choose in the recorder's check panel, `await expect(…).toHaveText(…)` and the like | The test's window |
| **Assert a region** | `await expect(…).toMatchAriaSnapshot(…)` with the ARIA snapshot of the region you pick | The test's window |
| **Mock a request** | `await page.route(…)` that answers as the server answered a request the page made | The editor alone, at any stop |

From the editor, the first four need the pause bar, so a headed browser: turn headed runs on
([How a run starts](./editor-runs#how-a-run-starts)). At a headless stop, Piwi Picker's
[Runs window](./runs-window#code-from-a-stop) runs them through the page it watches. **Mock a request** works
headless too.

- **In VS Code**, they are behind **Write code…** in the line above the stopped line, after the controls, in its hover,
  in the palette while a stop offers them (**Piwi: Pick a locator at the stop**, **Piwi: Record at the stop**,
  **Piwi: Assert at the stop**, **Piwi: Assert a region at the stop**, **Piwi: Mock a request at the stop…**), and
  behind the status bar's `</>` item, **Piwi: Write code at the stop…**.
- **In a JetBrains IDE**,
  they are links in the inlay above the stopped line (by the same short names), in the gutter icon's menu, in the status
  bar item's menu, and under **Tools → Piwi → Run control** with the same titles as VS Code's palette.

None has a default key: bind one in **Preferences: Open Keyboard Shortcuts** or **Settings → Keymap** (search
`piwi`). A stop offers only the actions its reporter takes: with one that predates them, none.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/vscode-run-control-code.png" alt="VS Code: a test paused before it types a coupon; above the line, the controls then Write code…; at the line's end, Piwi: 1 match; at the top, the list of the requests the test made, to mock one">
  <figcaption>Mock a request lists the answers the test received; the line's locator matches one element on the paused page.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Where the code goes

The code goes on a new line above the stopped statement (the first line of a statement broken over lines), indented
for it, on the page in scope there (`this.page` in a page object), with the import of `expect` the file lacks, as one
edit that one undo takes away. A second action at the same stop goes above the same statement, under the first.
The running test goes on with the code it started with: the new lines run next time, which the first code of a run
says.

Nothing is written, and the editor says why, at a stop:

- outside a test's or a function's body, such as a test timeout stopped at its `test(` line;
- as the body of an `if`, `else`, `for`, `while`, `do` or arrow function (`() => page.click(…)`) without braces,
  or on a line where no statement starts;
- in a file written on disk since the run started, or unsaved as it started: Piwi follows a file through the edits
  the editor makes, not through another program's;
- that the test went on from: an action answers the stop it was offered at.

Assert and Assert a region check this before anything opens in the test's window. Code that arrives while you type in
its file is not written into the changed text: a warning offers **Copy the code**.

## Mock a request

In a run Piwi started, each worker keeps the text answers its test's pages received for `fetch` and
XHR requests, the latest 50, 256 KB each at most, in its memory only. **Mock a request** lists them, the latest first,
by method and URL (type to filter on the URL), with the status, the type, the size (`no size` when the response did
not say) and when it finished in the test. Only the answer you choose is read whole:

```ts
await page.route('**/api/shipping?country=FR', (route) =>
  route.fulfill({
    json: {
      "price": 4.9,
      "token": "<hidden>"
    },
  }),
);
```

It is written as [Piwi Picker's Network tab](./mock-requests#mock-this-response) writes one, the body inline whatever
its size, with what it hides:

- **Credentials.** A field named like a password, a token, a key, a signature or a session is written as `<hidden>`,
  whatever it holds, and so is a value shaped like a credential anywhere in the body, by the
  [rule Piwi Picker's mocks follow](./mock-requests#mock-this-response): ids, hashes and cursors stay. The URL pattern
  matches such a value with a wildcard, and keeps the host. The list hides them too. Headers, cookies included, are
  never written.
- **Warnings.** The editor says how many values it wrote as `<hidden>`, that a body neither JSON nor a form was
  written as it came (read it before you commit it), and that a body seems to hold an email address or a phone
  number (replace it with made-up data).

## The locator at the cursor

While a test is stopped, put the cursor on a line of the stopped file: its end says how many elements the line's
locator matches on the stopped page, `Piwi: 3 matches`, `1 match` or `no match`, and where the pause bar shows, the
matches are outlined in the page. Edit the locator and it is counted again. The outline goes
when the cursor leaves the file or the test goes on.

The locator must start from the page the test stopped on, as the code written there would: a line of `adminPage` at a
stop on `page` may be another page, and says so for a moment instead of a count. Only the stopped file's lines are
counted, and a line without a locator says nothing.

## A failure

When its run [holds a failing test](./watch-a-run#hold-failures) (with breakpoints or a `page.pause()`, from its
start unless [your run options](./editor-runs#how-a-run-starts) choose otherwise, or once you turn it on with **Piwi:
Turn hold failures on or off for the run**, **Tools → Piwi → Run control → Turn hold failures on** or **off**, or Piwi Picker's
[Runs window](./runs-window)), the editor shows the failure as a stop of its own, at the line where the error entered
the test's code, or at the call a test timeout cut short:

`Held at its failure · Timed out 5000ms waiting for getByRole('button', { name: 'Apply' }) · attempt 2`  Resume  Pick  Record …

Its line is marked in red. **Resume** lets the test end as it failed (**Step** and **Finish** do the same, so the status
menu offers Resume alone); **Pick** replaces the failing locator, **Record** writes the steps that were missing
above the failing line, and the code actions work as at any stop. A failure its run does not hold goes on at once,
and the editor shows nothing of it.

## Limits

- **Runs Piwi started, and those [that follow your editor](./terminal-runs)**, with a reporter that takes the actions;
  an editor extension older than the reporter holds no failure.
- **A desktop reproduction's** code is [to copy](./desktop-runs#a-reproduction-in-your-editor).
- **Assert offers what a recording's check panel offers**: a value, a text, a name, visible or hidden, enabled or
  disabled, with no `toBeChecked` or `toHaveCount` choice.
- **Assert a region** leaves out the value of a password, one-time code or card field, in a shadow root too, and a link
  whose URL holds a credential.
- **Mock a request** knows `fetch` and XHR answers with a text body only; one the browser no longer holds cannot be
  mocked, which the editor says.
- **The count needs a locator Piwi reads**: literal arguments, starting from a page in scope on the line.

# Debug in my editor

On a failed execution's page, **Debug in my editor** takes you from the failure to the same test, stopped at the
failing line in your editor, on your machine. It sits on the **Source** tab, beside the open link of the frame where
the failure enters your code (a page object's line included), in the captured frames and in the full stack alike.

1. Click it. The dashboard hands your editor its [open link](./ide-integration) with `debug=1`: the Piwi plugin of a
   JetBrains IDE, or the Piwi extension in VS Code, Cursor or VSCodium, as your **Open in editor** method picks
   ([Auto](./ide-integration#auto-the-first-method-that-works) asks the plugin first).
2. The editor opens the failing line, then asks in a notification, never a dialog: **Debug this test here? Piwi runs
   “Checkout › pays” in the Playwright project “chromium”, headed, one worker, and stops at line 16.** Nothing runs
   until you click **Debug**.
3. Piwi runs that test alone, found in its spec by its title, in the Playwright project it failed in, headed, with
   `--workers=1` and your breakpoints, and stops at the failing line. From there the
   [controls](./editor-run-control) apply, and so does [Code from a pause](./editor-stop-code).
4. When the instance holds a [locator healing](./locator-healing) for the failure, the **Locator fix** panel's
   recommended locator is counted on the stopped page and outlined there, and the editor says so:
   **Piwi's suggested locator: getByTestId('pay') (outlined on the page).** While the cursor stays on the stopped line,
   its end says the same, and the outline stays. Without an instance, or a recommendation, the run only stops.

## From the editor

The same run starts from the editor, with no question: **Debug with Piwi** on a failure of the Piwi panel's
failures (its context menu in VS Code, the tool window's in a JetBrains IDE), and **Debug with Piwi** among a failed
test's actions in its gutter ([Runs from the editor](./editor-runs)).

## The stop is the run's alone

The failing line is a breakpoint of that one run, never one of your editor's: your breakpoint list stays as it was.
Once the test stopped there, the run drops it, so a retry, or a later call on that line, runs on. Breakpoints you set
or remove meanwhile apply as in any run, the failing line kept until the stop.

## What a link may ask

A link is anyone's to write, so the editor reads it as data, never as a command:

- The files must be in the window's folders (VS Code) or an open project (JetBrains IDE) once every symbolic link is
  followed, and under a Playwright config's folder: the failing line's a script file, the test's a spec.
- The line and the execution are positive whole numbers. The title and the project are plain text: no control
  character, no `[`, `]`, `<`, `>`, backtick or backslash, and a project name no shell expands. A field named twice
  refuses the link.
- A refused link opens and runs nothing, and says why. The command is built by the editor service from the test it
  finds in your spec, as for every run Piwi starts.

A JetBrains IDE also answers only a page of the instance a project is connected to, or of the desktop app, as for
Open in editor.

## Limits

- **The test as your spec has it.** The title must name one test of the spec as saved: a test renamed since the run is
  not found, and two of that title in describe blocks the dashboard does not name are refused. A title written with
  `${…}` parts matches with any text in their place, but one made of such parts alone matches nothing; Piwi passes the
  run's title as `--grep` too, so of the tests the line declares, only those whose title holds it run.
- **The line as your file has it.** The failing line is the run's: when the file changed since, the run stops at that
  line's number, or not at all when nothing there stops; a failure before it holds the test, as in any run with
  breakpoints.
- **Piwi's own editor clients.** The `vscode://file` and `jetbrains://` links, and IDE Remote Control, carry no
  `debug=1`. VS Code hands the link to its window focused last.
- **Not on a phone.** The button is hidden below the tablet width.

## Privacy

The link carries the failing file and line, the test's spec and title, its Playwright project and the execution's id,
from your browser to your editor on the same machine: through your operating system (VS Code), or the IDE's built-in
server on `127.0.0.1` (JetBrains). The suggested locator comes from the instance the editor is connected to.

# Failures in the editor

The [editor extensions](./editors) show the failures of the latest CI run at the lines that failed, lay your local runs
over them, and follow each failing line through your edits until a run covers its test again.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/vscode-failures.png" alt="VS Code: the failing tests marked in a spec, and the Failures view below">
  <figcaption>The failing tests in the spec, and the Failures view with the run you made since.</figcaption>
</figure>

## CI failures in the Problems panel

The failures of the latest complete [CI run](/reference/test-metadata#run-origin) on the checked-out branch, else the
default branch, are in the Problems panel, at the line that failed: the call in the error's stack when that file
is in your workspace (often a page object), else the `test(…)` line, with the failure's headline. In the spec, the
line a failing test failed at is tinted darker, with **✗ Failed here**, the
reason unless a Piwi problem says it, and **Run with Piwi** above it; the failure's screenshot and trace are among the
test's actions.

On a failure, the light bulb lists Piwi's quick fixes, each under Piwi's name. They edit the code; running
the test, its trace, the context for an agent, its page in the dashboard, the desktop app's jobs and **File an issue**
are on the failure's node in the [failures view](#the-failures-view), and running it above the line a spec failed at:

- **heal with …** makes the edit an [auto-heal pull request](/features/auto-heal) would, when
  [locator healing](/features/locator-healing) has a recommendation for the failing locator.
- **Run with Piwi** comes first once you rewrote the line it failed at, to check the edit.
- **apply the fix plan, then run its verification**, when the failure's [cluster](/features/failure-clusters) has a
  [fix plan](/features/fix-plans) whose patch applies to your files: the edit is previewed, then the plan's verify
  command runs in a terminal.

Hover for the error message, its call chain, the failure screenshot, the tickets linked to its cluster or test, and a
link to the failure in the dashboard. Over the error's marker, the marker's own text above them says what failed and in
which run; elsewhere on the line, or with no marker, the hover says it first. **File an issue**, on the failure's node,
opens its cluster in the dashboard to file one, or names the ticket already linked.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/vscode-hover.png" alt="VS Code: the hover on a failing line, dragged taller: the CI failure with its error, its call log and the chain of calls that reached the line, then the failure screenshot of the checkout page">
  <figcaption>The hover on a failing line: the error, how the test got there, and the page at the failure.</figcaption>
</figure>

A failure of a run on the checked-out branch is an error; one from another branch, such as the default branch's while
yours has no run yet, is a warning; one whose line you changed since the run is an information (a weak warning in a
JetBrains IDE). The `piwi.failureSeverity` setting (**Settings → Tools → Piwi → In the editor** in a JetBrains IDE) chooses
`warning` or `information` in place of the error, or `off`: nothing in the Problems panel, while the failures view,
the gutter and the lines above the tests (unless `piwi.codeLens` hides them) still show the failures.

## Your local runs

A later finished run on the branch, from the editor, `piwi run`, `npx playwright test` or the desktop app, overlays the
latest CI run per test and Playwright project: a test it fixed leaves the Problems panel, its lens saying *fixed locally
in run #124*; a test failing in it is an error that starts *Local failure:* and names *local run #124*, or *your run
#124* when this editor started it. The editor reads a run within a second of its end: [After a
run](./editor-runs#after-a-run).

## Failures follow your edits

A run reports the line a test failed at in the files it ran. The editor reads those files as the run saw them and
follows each failing line through your changes, saved or not:

- Add or remove lines above a failing line, and its error moves with it, in the Problems panel, the lines above the
  test and the failures view.
- Rewrite the failing line, and the error turns into an information marker, *Edited since run #120: …*: the run said
  nothing about the new line. The reason above the line reads *✎ edited since run #120*. The test keeps its failing mark
  until a run says otherwise.
- Delete the test, and its failure leaves the editor.

The next run that covers the test says what is true: a failure there is an error again, and a pass takes it away.

For a CI run, the files as the run saw them are those of its commit (`git show`); for a local run, a run without a
commit, or a commit your clone lacks, the files as saved when the editor first showed the failure.

## The failures view

The latest run's failures as a tree: the **Failures** view of the **Piwi** panel in VS Code, the Piwi tool window in a
JetBrains IDE. Its first node is the run, `Run #120 · CI · feature/x · 3 failing · 1 fixed locally`, with its age, or
the progress of your run, `running 4 of 9`. Under it:

- **Your runs since** lists the runs laid over it, such as `#124 · your run · 2 min ago · 1 passed, 0 failed`; a click
  opens one in the dashboard.
- The failures, grouped by spec (the default), by [failure cluster](/features/failure-clusters), by owner, or flat:
  **Group the failures by…**, in the view's title bar or the tool window's toolbar. The choice is kept for the
  workspace, and each group counts its failures.
- A failure shows its title, where it failed (`tests/login.spec.ts:42 · chromium · new`), and an icon for failing,
  edited since the run, or fixed locally, with its run (`your run #124`, `edited since run #120`), its headline in the
  hover.
- **Flaky in this run**: tests that passed on a retry, with [Flake Lab](./flake-lab)'s rate (`flaky 18%`). A test's
  menu offers its Flakiness tab and Flake Lab's commands (**Look into this flake…** in VS Code); the status bar's
  **Show the run's flaky tests** opens the group.

In a workspace with several Playwright configs, each config with a run, your runs or failures has a node of its own,
named by its folder (`apps/admin`), with its project and counts beside it (`Admin · 2 failing`), over its tree as
above. Its row in VS Code, and its context menu in both
editors, re-run that config's failing tests (**Re-run the failing tests**) and open its run in the dashboard; the
context menu adds **Compare with…** for that config. With one config, the run is the first node.

Click a failure (double-click, Enter or **Next Occurrence** in a JetBrains IDE) to open its line. **Run with Piwi**,
**Open the trace** and **Open in dashboard** sit on its row in VS Code; the context menu adds **Go to the test**,
**Debug with Piwi**, **Verify ×3 with Piwi**, **Open the screenshot**, **Copy context for agent**, and **File an
issue** on a failure with a [cluster](/features/failure-clusters). While the
[desktop app](/features/desktop#jobs-from-your-editor) runs, it adds **Reproduce in the desktop app** and **Find the
breaking commit in the desktop app** on a CI failure, and **Run Flake Lab on its untested suspects in the desktop app**
on a failure whose test has an untested [flake suspect](./flake-lab); **Share on …** in a job's notification records
its result. **Heal** stays a quick fix on the line.

The title bar, or the toolbar, holds Refresh the latest run, **Re-run the failing tests** (every config's), **Open the
latest run** (the run the status bar shows; **Open in dashboard** in a JetBrains IDE, the page of the selected failure
or run), **Compare with…** (for the active file's config) and the grouping. In VS Code, **Follow the active editor**, in
the `…` menu, selects the first failure of the file you switch to until **Stop following the active editor**, and the
badge counts the failing tests, as the tool window's title and its icon's red dot do. The JetBrains tool window's gear
menu keeps Connect, Piwi Picker's pairing, the MCP configurations, **Read the instance and the configs again**, the
settings and **Open the documentation**. The tree is read again when a run ends or an edit moves a failure.

With no failure to list, the view says why, in both editors: no failure in the run read; no run yet, or none for the
baseline chosen, with **Compare with…**; an instance that does not answer, naming it and why, with **Retry** (also retried on
its own); a desktop app to restart or update; an API key refused or missing, or no project, with **Connect…** and
**Open settings**; an instance still being read; or no connection, with **Connect…**. **Re-run the failing tests**
stays while failures are listed, the instance answering or not.

## Related

- [The editor's status bar](./editor-status-bar#compare-with-another-run): choose the run the failures are read against.
- [Runs from the editor](./editor-runs): run the failing tests again, and follow the run in the status bar.
- [Locator healing](/features/locator-healing): where the heal quick fix comes from.

# Coverage in the editor

With [coverage](/guide/concepts#coverage) recorded, the [editor extensions](./editors) mark the lines of an
application file your tests ran, the executable lines no test runs, and the lines you changed since, in VS Code and
the JetBrains IDEs, Rider included. A lens above each function names the tests that ran it and runs them; the hover on
a line lists them.

## Turn it on

The marks show what the reporter records, per test:

- **Server code**: an ASP.NET Core or Nitro backend built for coverage, with the reporter's `coverage.server` set to `lines`, or
  `PIWI_COVERAGE_SERVER=lines`: [Server coverage](./server-coverage) has the steps. With `functions`,
  every line of a function that ran is marked run, and no line is marked as not run.
- **Browser code**: recorded per file ([code reach](./code-reach#turn-it-on)), so such a file lists its tests in its
  top lens, with no line marks; with `coverage.browser: 'functions'`, every line of a function that ran is marked run,
  with its lens above it, and no line is marked as not run; with `'lines'`, its lines are marked as a server file's.

Nothing else is needed in the editor; test files and files without recorded coverage show no marks.

The editor asks the instance for a file's coverage when you open it (only a file code reach says coverage
recorded, when it can tell), on a refresh and when a run ends; the instance answers again only when it changed. Typing
asks nothing: the marks follow your edits locally.

## The marks

| Mark          | Meaning                                                                                                                  |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Solid, teal   | A test ran the line. The hover names the tests.                                                                          |
| Solid, slate  | The line is executable and no test runs it. Shown when the run recorded the file's executable lines, which `lines` does. |
| Dashed, amber | The line changed since the coverage run: what runs it is not known until a run records it again.                         |
| Solid, orange | In a file no test reaches, the line changed since the default branch: an [uncovered change](#uncovered-changes).         |

Teal and slate are the colors the dashboard marks a file's source in. The hover on a marked line ends by saying what
the marks mean.

In VS Code the marks are a bar at the left edge of each line, in `piwi.coverageRunBorder`, `piwi.coverageNotRunBorder`,
`piwi.coverageChangedBorder` and `piwi.uncoveredChangeBorder`, which a theme or `workbench.colorCustomizations` can
restyle; all but the lines run also show in the overview ruler. In a JetBrains IDE they are in the gutter, beside the
IDE's own coverage, and, all but the lines run, in the scroll bar; hovering either shows what the lines are and what
the marks mean; a click on a run mark runs the tests that ran its line, and on any mark goes to the next line no test
runs, hides the marks or edits their colors (**Settings → Editor → Color Scheme → Piwi → Coverage**: the error stripe color is the
mark's, and a background tints the lines).

## Changed since the coverage run

Coverage names the lines of one version of a file, by its git blob id, the id `git hash-object` gives the file as the
test ran it. Your file may be another version: edited since, or the coverage may come from a CI run on an older commit.
The marks come from, in order:

1. **The version that is your file as it stands**, saved or not, whatever its line endings and byte order mark: its
   marks are exact.
2. **The version your file was saved as**, when you edited it since.
3. **The version the most tests recorded that your repository holds** (`git cat-file`).

From the second and the third, the lines are placed on your file through the diff between the two, as
[failures follow your edits](./editor-failures#failures-follow-your-edits): a line moved by the edits above it keeps its
mark on its new line; a line the diff adds or rewrites is marked changed since the coverage run, not guessed; a line it
removes loses its mark. Blank lines are never marked changed.

When your repository holds none of the versions, such as a commit you have not fetched, no line is marked and the
file's lens says `coverage recorded on another version`. Fetching it brings the marks back on the next refresh.

## Uncovered changes

A file the editor can observe and no test reaches has its changes marked before the pull request's
[uncovered changes](./uncovered-changes) list them: a page (Nuxt `pages/**`) while the locator index knows the pages
your tests act on, or a server route (`server/api/**`, `server/routes/**`) while code reach maps routes to tests, that
no test's locator acts on, requests or runs. The rule is close to the pull request's, not the same: it applies no
coverage scope and no window of runs, and a page a test only visited reads as unreached. Its lines changed since the default branch are marked orange: those added since
the commit your branch left it at (the merge base with `origin/main`, else `main`), uncommitted changes included,
blank lines left out. The file's top lens says `Uncovered changes: 12 lines changed since main, and no test reaches
this file`, and opens the file's gaps on the dashboard's Coverage tab, where **Accept** copies a draft test once a
pull-request run has raised one. The hover on a marked line says the same. A test that reaches the file, or the change reaching the default
branch, takes the marks away. A file nothing can observe, and a project whose code reach is missing or cut short, show
nothing.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/vscode-uncovered.png" alt="VS Code: a server route no test reaches, its lines changed since main marked orange, the top lens and the hover saying why">
  <figcaption>A server route no test requests: the lines changed since <code>main</code> are marked, and the hover says why.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Lenses and hover

- **Top of the file**: `Reached by 6 tests · 1 failing · 41 of 63 lines run · 3 lines changed since the coverage run`.
  The tests are those code reach and the coverage name; the line counts show when the run recorded the executable
  lines. A click runs those tests.
- **Above each function a test ran**: `Reached by 2 tests · 1 failing`, the tests that ran it. A click runs them,
  as [Runs from the editor](./editor-runs#run-tests) describes.
- **Hover**: on a line tests ran, each test with its latest result and a link to its page in the dashboard; on a line
  no test runs, `no test runs this line`; on a changed line, that it changed since the coverage run.

## Refresh the marks with a local run

A run started from a lens of a server file records the backend's coverage by line: the editor adds
`PIWI_COVERAGE_SERVER=lines` to the run's environment, which the reporter reads when your Playwright config leaves
`coverage.server` unset. The backend the run calls must be the coverage build, as for any run that records server
coverage. From a browser file's lens, the run records the browser's coverage by function instead
(`PIWI_COVERAGE_BROWSER=functions`). When the run ends, the editor reads the file's coverage again, and the marks show what your run recorded:
exactly, as long as the file is as you saved it for the run, since the reporter takes blob ids from the files on disk.

A run started anywhere else (a test's lens, the failures view, a selection) changes nothing of your config's coverage
options.

## Show or hide the marks

**Piwi: Show or hide the coverage marks**, under **Tools → Piwi** in a JetBrains IDE, where a check mark says the
marks show.

The command shows up once a file showed marks. Shown by default, the choice is yours in every project,
the [setting](/reference/editor-settings#in-the-editor) `piwi.coverageMarks` in VS Code's user settings and the IDE's
own settings in a JetBrains IDE. The lenses and the hover stay.

## C# and Razor files

Both extensions read `.cs`, `.cshtml` and `.razor` files, so an ASP.NET Core project's services, controllers and views
show their marks and lenses as any application file does. The JetBrains plugin is verified for compatibility with Rider;
it starts once it finds a Playwright config in the solution's folder or its Git repository.

## Limits

- **Lines for server code only.** Browser code is recorded per file or per function; recorded per function, a function
  that ran marks all its lines run, the branches it skipped included.
- **The latest coverage of each test**: on your branch where its tests ran with coverage, else on the default branch.
- **API calls** through Playwright's `request` fixture keep their last response's server coverage only
  ([Server coverage](./server-coverage#limits)).
- An instance without coverage shows nothing, and is asked again only on a refresh.

## Related

- [Code reach](./code-reach): turning coverage on, and what it records
- [Editor extensions](./editors): what else the editors show
- [Runs from the editor](./editor-runs): running the tests a lens names
- [Uncovered changes](./uncovered-changes): the changed files no test reaches, on a pull request
