# Record a bug report

Reproduce a bug in your browser, say what the page should show, and get the test that proves it. A
[recording](./record-actions) of the [Piwi Picker extension](./extension) becomes a bug report as soon as you mark
something on the page as wrong ("this should read Total: 36.00"): it then hands you a failing Playwright test, a
Markdown report and a `.piwibug` file for the developer, with the evidence every recording collects. Everything is
built in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere unless you send it to your Piwi instance. This page covers marking what
is wrong and what a report holds, with no instance; [Replay a recording](./replay-a-bug-report) plays one again, and
[Bug reports on your instance](./bug-reports) covers what an instance does with one sent to it.

<figure>
  <video src="/videos/picker-report-loop.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline controls aria-label="Recording a bug on a cart page: a coupon applied, the total checked with what it should read instead of what it shows, then Finish opens the report with its steps, its evidence and a failing test to copy"></video>
  <figcaption>Reproduce it, say what the page should show, finish: the report and its failing test.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Marking what is wrong

Open the popup on the page where the flow starts, choose **Record** (`1`) as [Record a test](./record-actions)
describes, and reproduce the bug. These tools of the recording bar say what is wrong:

- **Check an element**: pick the element, then choose what to check: its text, its value or its name as screen readers
  announce it. The dialog shows what the page shows now and an **Expected** field holding the same value: type what it
  should be instead. For a state, choose the one the element should be in and is not, such as **It should be hidden**
  or **It should be grayed out, not usable**.
- **Check the address**: type the path the flow should have reached, such as `/checkout/thanks`, in place of the one
  the page is on.
- **Something is missing**: say what should be there (a button, a link, a title, a text field, a dropdown, …) and its
  name, such as a button named "Download invoice". Piwi Picker looks for it on the page first and refuses one that is
  there already; use Check an element for that one.

Before you press **Add the check**, the dialog says which of the two it will record: a check that passes, or the page
marked as wrong, which makes the recording a bug report whose test fails until the page shows what you expect. Once it
is wrong, a **Note** field takes what happened, in your words. Each becomes a step of the recording, in place, with what
the page showed. **Finish** ends the recording and opens the report.

## Evidence

Every recording keeps, whether or not anything is marked wrong:

- **Console errors and warnings**, uncaught errors and unhandled promise rejections, with the page they happened on.
- **Failed requests**: the method, the path, and the status of any request that failed or answered 400 or more: in
  Chrome and Edge, documents, scripts and images included; elsewhere, the page's `fetch` and `XMLHttpRequest` calls. Query values are removed (`/api/cart/coupon?code=<redacted>`), ids and tokens in the path are collapsed
  as Piwi does for routes, and no header or body is ever read.
- **An outline of the page** around the element marked wrong, or of the page at **Finish** when nothing was: roles,
  names, states and field values, in the YAML form Playwright's ARIA snapshots use, at most 400 lines. Piwi Picker
  builds it from its own reading of the page, so it is an outline, not Playwright's snapshot. Password fields, and
  fields for a card number, its security code or a one-time code, never show their value.
- **Screenshots**, when something is marked wrong, at **Finish** and when you ask for one, three at most.
- **A screenshot of each step**: the page as the step began, with the element it acts on, for whoever has to
  [play that step by hand](./replay-a-bug-report#when-a-step-cannot-be-played). They show the whole page: leave them out
  in the report if they show what should not be shared. Taken through the debugging protocol, so mostly in Chrome and
  Edge.
- **The context**: the page, the browser and its version, the time and the extension's version.
- **The viewport size**: at the start, then after each resize or zoom change, with the zoom when it is not 100%. The
  test sets it with `page.setViewportSize` before the step it applies from, so a bug seen on a narrow window
  reproduces at that width.

The first 100 console entries and 100 failed requests are kept; the report counts the rest.

### How the evidence is collected

In Chrome and Edge, Piwi Picker reads the console, the requests and the screenshots of the tab the recording started
in through the browser's [debugging protocol](./extension#the-debugging-bar), from the page's first script, on every
page of the recording. Chrome's debugging bar shows from the start until you finish; the recording bar says it is
expected, and adds a **Screenshot** button.

Elsewhere (Firefox, the site's other tabs, or once the bar is cancelled), a small script added to the page itself
wraps `console.error`, `console.warn`, `fetch` and `XMLHttpRequest` without changing what they do, under the same site
access as recording, and is removed when you finish or discard the recording. A screenshot then needs the `activeTab`
grant: it works from the click that started the recording until the tab moves to another page; after that, open Piwi
Picker on the tab and choose **Take a screenshot** (`S`), which takes Replay's place in the popup while a recording
runs.

## The report

**Finish** opens the recording's [finish panel](./record-actions#the-finish-panel) as a report: a title to write, the
steps with the wrong ones highlighted, and a line summing up the evidence.

- **Copy failing test**, in place of **Copy test**, copies a Playwright spec for your suite, marked `test.fail()` so it
  keeps your CI green while the bug exists, tagged `@bug`, with paths instead of the recorded URLs, the most stable
  locator recorded for each element and, with a connection, calls to your test functions. What it holds, and what to
  do once it passes: [The failing test](./bug-reports#the-failing-test).
- **Copy report** copies the report as Markdown, for an issue or a message: the steps in plain words, what was
  expected and what the page showed, the notes, the console entries, the failed requests and the outline.
- **Download .piwibug** saves it all as one [file](/reference/bug-report-file), which Replay and the
  [desktop app](./desktop#importing-local-files) open. It is a zip archive: rename it to `.zip` to look inside, or to
  attach it to a GitHub issue. [`piwi codegen`](/reference/cli#codegen) renders its `steps.json` for any project.

Typed values stay as you typed them, except passwords, card numbers, their security codes and one-time codes, which
are never recorded: the spec reads them from an environment variable. Look over the report before you share it.

With the extension connected to an instance, **Send to Piwi…** sends the report after a preview. It shows once a step
is marked wrong: a recording that marks nothing wrong is no bug report. See
[Sending a report](./bug-reports#sending-a-report).

## Replaying a report

**Replay**, on the finished report or from the popup (`R`), plays the steps again in a tab and says whether the bug
shows there: see [Replay a recording](./replay-a-bug-report).

## Limits

- It follows one site, like any [recording](./record-actions), in the top-level document only.
- Without the debugging protocol, only the page's own `fetch` and `XMLHttpRequest` calls are seen: not images,
  stylesheets, a form that loads a new page, or a request made by a worker.
- A recording sends nothing anywhere: only **Send to Piwi…** does, after showing what it sends.

## Related

- [Record a test](./record-actions): the recording, its bar and its finish panel
- [Replay a recording](./replay-a-bug-report): playing a report again, in the browser or with Playwright
- [Steps file](/reference/steps-format): the format of `steps.json`
- [Bug report file](/reference/bug-report-file): what a `.piwibug` holds
- [CLI: codegen](/reference/cli#codegen): a steps file rendered as a spec for your project
- [Browser extension](./extension): every tool of Piwi Picker

# Replay a recording

**Replay** plays a [recording](./record-actions)'s steps again in a tab, with a cursor that moves to each element and a
caption saying what it does, then says whether each still finds its element and, for a [bug report](./report-a-bug),
whether the bug shows there. It suits the developer who receives a report: open the app on your own dev server, and
the steps run there, with your session and your browser's developer tools at hand, or
[with Playwright](#running-it-with-playwright) in the desktop app.

<figure>
  <video src="/videos/picker-replay-loop.mp4" autoplay loop muted playsinline controls aria-label="Replaying a bug report on a cart page: the cursor fills the coupon, clicks Apply and checks the total, and the verdict says the bug shows here, the total reading 50 instead of 45"></video>
  <figcaption>The report's four steps played again, then the verdict: reproduced.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Choosing a recording

- From a recording's [finish panel](./record-actions#the-finish-panel), **Replay** plays it at once on the same site.
- From the popup, **Replay** (`R`) asks for the site's access if needed, then for what to play: the recording just made
  in this browser, a bug report or not, a [`.piwibug` file](/reference/bug-report-file) (or the same file named `.zip`)
  or its `steps.json`, the text of a `steps.json` pasted in, or, connected, one of the project's reports on Piwi.
- From a failed execution on the dashboard, **Export → Bug report (.piwibug)** makes a report from the test run
  ([below](#a-report-made-from-a-test-run)), and **Steps (steps.json)** copies its steps to paste.

The steps run on the tab's site, whichever site they were recorded on. A step that opens its page in a new tab, such as
a link that opens an order beside the list, takes the replay to that tab, as the recording went on there.

## The answer

Each element is looked for with every locator it was recorded with, the one the test uses first. When that
one finds nothing for two seconds, finds several elements, or finds one the other locators disagree on, the element
most of them agree on is used, and the step says which locator found it: a label that changed or an id made up on each load does not stop
the replay. The element is then waited for as Playwright waits: visible, enabled and still, for as long as Playwright
waits or, when you waited longer for it while recording (a reply that takes the server fifteen seconds), that long and
a few seconds more, up to a minute. The replay ends with one of five answers:

- **Reproduced**: a step marked wrong, or a recording's check, does not hold, such as a total that still reads
  "Total: 40.00", and the panel says whether that is the value reported.
- **Not reproduced**: every expected result holds here.
- **Could not reach the bug** (the dashboard's *diverged*): a step could not be played (it found no element, several,
  or a disabled one, or the flow ended on another page) and you stopped there, or a check that held when recorded
  fails. The data, the login or a flag differ here.
- **Failed at step 4, as in the test run**: in a report made from a test run, the step that could not be played is
  the one the test failed at.
- **Replayed every step**: the steps hold no check.

A recording that marks nothing wrong says **A check failed**, **Every check holds** or **Stopped at step 4: the page
went another way** for the first three.

Under the answer, the panel lists the failed requests and console errors the page showed during the replay, such as
"POST /api/cart/coupon answered 500": from the moment the replay started, never those of the recording, even when you
replay on the page you just recorded the report on. For a report from Piwi, **Share result…** records the answer on the report, with
the site it ran on, after showing what it sends.

**Step by step** waits for **Next** before each step, with the element outlined, so you can set a breakpoint first.

## When a step cannot be played

A step Replay cannot play is handed to you rather than ending the replay. The panel says why, names the step in words
and, when the report has [a screenshot of each step](./report-a-bug#evidence), shows the page as it began there, the
element outlined. It lists the locators the element was recorded with and outlines on the page every element they
still find, such as two buttons where the recording saw one, as the page changes. Do it yourself on the page, then
choose:

- **I did it, continue**: the replay goes on with the next step, even when your action loaded another page or opened
  one in a new tab.
- **Skip this step**: it goes on without it.
- **Stop here**: it ends there, and says it could not reach the bug.

A password, or a card number, its security code or a one-time code, is never in a report, nor what was typed when
the sender left the typed values out: Replay hands that step to you to type it. A click or a key the page never got is handed to you too: a browser dialog in front of the tab, such as
Chrome's warning about a password found in a data breach after a login, takes the input. Close it, then do the step. A hover recorded without any locator is skipped, since the next step points at its own element.

Under the answer, the panel lists the steps played by hand.

## A report made from a test run

A `.piwibug` exported from a failed execution holds the test's steps up to the failure and its failing assertion;
what the run did not keep enough of to play becomes a [manual step](/reference/steps-format#manual-steps), which Replay
hands to you as above, with the line of the test it stands for, in Piwi Picker's language. Calls that are not steps at
all are listed in the report's Markdown under **Not replayed**.

When the test failed on an action rather than on an assertion, the report says which step; reaching it and failing
there answers **Failed at step N, as in the test run**, and playing it answers **Not reproduced**.

A test run does not keep the page each step happened on once a click may have opened another, so Replay does not
follow such a step into a new tab: it stays in the tab it started in, and a step the test played in a popup is handed
to you.

## Trusted input

In Chrome and Edge, Replay sends trusted input as Playwright does, through the
[debugging protocol](./extension#the-debugging-bar): a real hover, clicks, keys and drags that the page cannot tell
from a person's, under Chrome's debugging bar until the replay ends. In Firefox, when the browser refuses the session,
once the bar is cancelled, or once the browser refuses one of its commands (the bar then closes), Replay goes on with
the page's own events; the panel says which, step by step.

A report names the files a step chose but never carries them: Replay asks you to choose them, or to skip the step.

With trusted input, each step plays at the viewport size it was recorded at, in CSS pixels whatever your zoom, and the
tab gets its own size back when the replay ends. Otherwise the panel says when the window's size differs from the recorded one, so you can resize it.

## Running it with Playwright

For the exact verdict and a trace, the [desktop app](./desktop) runs a report's steps with Playwright in your project,
once Piwi Picker is [paired with it](./extension-connection#pair-with-the-desktop-app). **Run with Playwright…**, in
Replay's chooser beside **Start** or on a finished replay, shows what it sends (the title and the steps, with the
values typed in them) and sends it on **Send**. The request holds steps, never code. The app's window shows it with
the steps in words, the linked project to run it in, and the flags (headed and a trace by default, a Playwright
project, a repeat count). Nothing runs before **Run with Playwright**; **Decline** drops it, and a request left
unanswered expires after ten minutes.

The app writes the spec to run, with the project's settings, to `piwi-repro/bug-<id>.spec.ts` under the test directory
your Playwright config names, runs it in the **Local runs** tray with the project's own config, and deletes it when the
run ends. The verdict, read from where the test failed, goes back to Piwi Picker: **reproduced** when an expected
result does not hold, **not reproduced** when the test passes, or **diverged** at the step that failed first.

## Limits

- It plays one site, in the top-level document only, as the recording was made. A step that opens another site, or
  an address that is not a web page, is handed to you.
- **Share result…** and **Run with Playwright…** are the only parts that send anything, each after showing what it
  sends.

- [Record a bug report](./report-a-bug): marking what the page gets wrong
- [Bug reports on your instance](./bug-reports): the reports kept

# Bug reports on your instance

A tester who [records a bug report](./report-a-bug) in Piwi Picker can send it to your Piwi instance. Piwi keeps it
with its steps and the evidence the tester chose to send; writes it as a failing Playwright test for your project; and
follows that test's runs: from the test being committed, to the bug looking fixed, to the report closing when the fix
holds. This page covers what needs an instance: sending a report, the failing test (the one
Piwi Picker copies too), and following it to the fix. Recording a report is on
[Record a bug report](./report-a-bug), and playing one again, in the browser or with Playwright, on
[Replay a recording](./replay-a-bug-report).

## Sending a report

With the extension [connected to the instance](./extension-connection), the finished report offers
**Send to Piwi…**. It opens a preview of exactly what leaves the browser, for the project the tab's address maps to:

- the title and the steps, with the values typed during the recording (never a password, which is not recorded);
- one box per kind of evidence: the screenshots, the [screenshot of each step](./report-a-bug#evidence), the console
  errors and warnings, the failed requests (method, path and status, never a body) and the outline of the page;
- **Leave out the values I typed**, which removes them from the steps and from the evidence that repeats them; the
  failing test then reads them from environment variables.

Nothing is sent before **Send**, and only to the connected instance. Anyone who can read a project can send a report to it, so a tester's own key is enough.

The report keeps the language it was written in; the test Piwi writes from it is the same in every language.

## The report's page

**Bug reports**, in a project's **More actions** menu and in the command palette on its pages, lists them newest
first, by status. A report's page says what the
tester expected and what the page showed instead, where the report stands, and what to do next, with these tabs:

- **Steps**: the steps in words, each marked step with its expected result, the value the page showed and the note.
- **Evidence**: the screenshots, the page as each step began with its element outlined, the failed requests, the
  console entries and the page's outline.
- **Reproductions**: each time someone replayed it or ran it with Playwright and shared what they found (**Share
  result…** in Piwi Picker).
- **Spec**: the failing test.

**Dismiss** sets a report aside: runs no longer move it. **Reopen** brings it back.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/bug-report.png" alt="A bug report's page: situation, state, next step and why the suite missed it, over its steps">
  <figcaption>A report's page.</figcaption>
</figure>

### Why the suite missed it

The page also says, in one line, why no test caught the bug, from the [locators your tests use](./locator-usage) on
the report's page: "4 tests visit /cart; 2 reach the element marked, and none asserts its text". **Show the tests**
lists them, and the owner is the one of the spec file whose tests visit the page most (its `piwi:owner`, else
CODEOWNERS). It needs the [capture fixtures](/guide/capture-fixtures), which record the page each locator ran on.

Until a test names it, an open report is also an **escaped defect** on the [Test Map](./scenario-gaps): one blind spot
per page with open reports, ranked like any gap. A report closed while no test names it becomes a gap of its own,
*fixed without a regression test*, and every report of the last 180 days raises the escape history of the gaps on its
page ([exposure](/reference/gap-detectors#exposure)).

## The failing test

A report's failing test, the one Piwi Picker's **Copy failing test** gives and the one the **Spec** tab shows, is
written by one converter, also [`piwi codegen`](/reference/cli#codegen)'s: the `@bug` tag, paths instead of the
recorded site's URLs so your `baseURL` applies, the most stable locator recorded for each element, a URL check after
each step that leads to another page, the recorded viewport sizes, and the value the page showed beside the marked
assertion, as a comment. Marked `test.fail()`, it passes while the bug exists and keeps your CI green; once the bug is
fixed, Playwright reports the expected failure as a failure: remove `test.fail()` and the test guards the fix.

The **Spec** tab adds what Piwi knows about your project: calls to your [test functions](./test-functions) where the
steps match one, as Piwi Picker's copy has them once connected, and for each element the locator your tests already use
when it is not [brittle](/reference/locator-stability), which is why its `getByLabel('Coupon')` below reads
`getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Coupon' })` in the copy Piwi Picker makes. Two versions:

- **To commit**: marked `test.fail()`, with a `piwi:bug` annotation naming the report.
- **To run**: the same test without `test.fail()` or the annotation, which fails on the expected result while the bug
  is there.

```ts
test('bug: coupon not applied to the total', {
  tag: ['@bug'],
  annotation: [{ type: 'piwi:bug', description: '37' }],
}, async ({ page }) => {
  test.fail(); // passes while the bug exists; remove this line with the fix
  await page.goto('/cart');
  await page.getByLabel('Coupon').fill('SPRING10');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Apply coupon' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('cart-total')).toHaveText('Total: 36.00'); // recorded: 'Total: 40.00'
});
```

Two project settings shape it, under **Generated specs** in the **Source control** section of the project's **Settings**
tab: the folder bug specs go to (`tests/bugs` by default) and the module `test` and `expect` are imported from, such as
`../fixtures` when your tests use fixtures of their own.

From a terminal, [`piwi bug 37 --write`](/reference/cli#bug) writes the spec into that folder and runs it once.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/bug-report-spec.png" alt="A bug report's Spec tab: the failing Playwright test written from the report's steps, ready to commit">
  <figcaption>A report's Spec tab: the failing test, written with the project's settings.</figcaption>
</figure>

## From report to fix

Once a test naming the report (`piwi:bug 37`) runs on the default branch, the report follows it (the run `piwi bug --write`
starts moves nothing):

| Status | When |
|---|---|
| **Open** | Sent; no run has carried a test naming it yet. |
| **Test committed** | A test naming it ran and the bug still shows: with `test.fail()`, the test failed as expected. |
| **Looks fixed** | That test, still marked `test.fail()`, passed in every browser project that ran it. The run's [pull-request comment](./pr-feedback) says to remove `test.fail()` from its file, and the `bug.looks_fixed` [notification](/reference/notification-events) fires. |
| **Closed** | The test passed as an ordinary test, `test.fail()` removed: the fix holds. |

A closed report whose test fails again goes back to **Test committed**. A test marked `test.fail()` that passes is
never counted into a [failure cluster](./failure-clusters): it is good news about one test, shown as **Looks fixed** on
the run.

## Filing it in Jira

When the project is bound to Jira in its [issue tracking](./issue-tracking) settings, a report becomes a ticket in
three ways, all through the same outbox, links and attachments:

- **From the Send preview**: **Also create a Jira issue in SHOP** is offered to a sender who may create issues
  there (Contributor or above, or an administrator).
- **From the report's page**: **Create issue**, with the same modal as a failure cluster.
- **For every report**: **File every bug report**, in the project's two-way sync settings, files each report as it
  arrives, whoever sends it; the preview then says so.

The ticket carries the steps, what was expected and what the page showed, the evidence (the screenshots attached to
it), the failing test to commit, the reproductions and a link back, with the labels `piwi` and `piwi-bug-<id>`. It is
written in the binding's ticket language, whatever language the report was written in: the steps are written again in
that language, the reporter's own words (the title, the note, the values typed) stay as they were, and a line says which
language the report came in.

The ticket then follows the report: with **Comment on fix** and **Transition on fix** on, a report that looks fixed
comments on its ticket and moves it; with **Resolve on close** and **Reopen on ticket reopen**, the report closes and
reopens as its ticket moves into and out of Done.

## Running it with Playwright in the desktop app

Piwi Picker sends a report's steps to the [desktop app](./desktop), once
[paired with it](./extension-connection#pair-with-the-desktop-app), which runs them with Playwright in your project for
the exact verdict and a trace: see [Running it with Playwright](./replay-a-bug-report#running-it-with-playwright).

## Replaying a report from Piwi

A developer with the extension connected finds the project's open reports in Piwi Picker's **Replay**, beside the
file chooser: the report's steps play in their own tab, on their own dev server, and a step handed over shows its
screenshot. See [Replay a recording](./replay-a-bug-report).

## For agents

The [MCP server](./mcp) has `list_bug_reports`, `get_bug_report` (the steps in words, what was expected, the evidence
and the reproductions), `render_steps`, which writes a report's failing test, or any steps file's, and
`set_bug_report_status`, which dismisses, reopens or closes a report.

## Related

- [Record a bug report](./report-a-bug): recording a report in Piwi Picker
- [Steps files](/reference/steps-format): the format of the steps
- [Test metadata](/reference/test-metadata#ownership-metadata-piwi-annotations): the `piwi:bug` annotation

# Runs window

Piwi Picker's Runs window, a window of its own beside the test's browser, follows the runs VS Code, a JetBrains IDE
or the [desktop app](#the-desktop-app-s-runs) starts: it pauses, steps and resumes them, writes code from a stop through the editor and, for a headless or remote
test, shows its page live, takes your clicks and keys on it, and picks a locator on its image. The editor shows the
same stops: [Pause and step from the editor](./editor-run-control).

## Open it

With Piwi Picker [paired with VS Code or a JetBrains IDE](./editor-pairing), or with the
[desktop app](./extension-connection#pair-with-the-desktop-app), the popup shows a **Runs** tile under
**Tests**, muted with **Not connected** while none of them answers. It opens the Runs window where you left it last. While a test waits at a stop for you (a breakpoint, a **Pause**, a failure held
at its line, not a stop an agent drives), the tile says how many in the pause bar's violet, as do the toolbar's badge
and the Runs window's title (`1 waiting · Runs · Piwi Picker`); while none waits, how many failed, in red, a run that failed while
the Runs window was not in front counted until you bring it there. For each run
the editor [started](./editor-runs): its folder and command, how many of its tests ended (`3 of 9 tests · 1 failed`),
then each worker's test and whether it runs or where it stopped (the file and line, the call about to run, an image of
the page). A run that ended says how: passed, failed with its first
failure, timed out or interrupted. The count and the outcome need `@piwitests/reporter` newer than 0.67.0. A run
without [**Watch**](#watch-live) and no test stopped says how one stops: a breakpoint, a `page.pause()` or **Pause**. A run [started outside Piwi](./terminal-runs) shows too, marked **Terminal** or **Test runner**.
The CI runs in progress of the projects your [connection](./extension-connection) maps show, watched only, through
that instance, read again every 15 seconds while the window is open, with **Open** and their running tests, each with
**Watch** ([A CI run of your branch](./editor-ci-runs)): nothing steers them, except
[Pause, Resume, End the test](./pause-ci-test#where-it-shows) and [Let it go](./hold-ci-failure#where-it-shows), for
those who may control them.

## The controls

**Pause** stops a running test before its next call; while the test waits in a long one, its row says which (a
locator call, for how long), with [**End the test**](./end-the-test#while-a-pause-waits-for-a-call). At a stop, **Resume**, **Step**, **Finish** and
[**End the test**](./end-the-test) do what they do [in the editor](./editor-run-control#the-controls); Run to the cursor
stays in the editor. A live run of several workers shows one at a time, behind tabs marked with their state, with
**Pause all** and **Resume all** under its name. A new stop takes the tab from a worker neither stopped nor watched,
and **Resume** or **End the test** moves it to the next stopped test. **Stop the run** ends a run an editor or the
desktop app started, not a terminal's or test runner's. Resume, Step and Finish have
[keys](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts#piwi-picker-s-runs-window), and the
[run shortcut](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts#the-run-shortcut) resumes or pauses every run from any window.

While a run's [**Hold failures**](./watch-a-run#hold-failures), a switch on each run, is on, a failing test is held at
its line: **Failed at** in red, its error under it. **Resume** lets it end as it failed; **Pick** replaces the failing
locator.

**Share live**, under the run's name, shares the run with your team: [Share a local run live](./share-live).

### Who drives a stop

Each run names who else has it open (**Also open in the desktop app**, **An agent follows this run**), and each worker
who watches its page (**Watched by you and Visual Studio Code**). One tool drives a stop at a time: an agent that
paused it or acts on it, else the last whose person clicked, typed or picked there. While another tool drives it or an
agent follows the run, **Take control** makes it yours: an agent's actions there are refused, and the agent is told
the stop was taken, until you **Give back**, stop watching the page or close the tool. A person's **Resume**, **Step**
and **Finish** always answer the stop, and the stop a person's **Step** or run to the cursor comes to stays theirs. A stop an
agent asked for reads **Paused by the agent**.

## Code from a stop

The actions under **Code** (the last two in **More** once five show) send code to the editor, which writes it at the
stopped line, when its Piwi extension and your reporter take them. **Pick** and **Record** start the pause bar's **Pick
a locator** and **Record**, **Assert** the recorder's **Check an element**, and **Assert a region** a pick whose
ARIA snapshot becomes `toMatchAriaSnapshot`.
They run in the test's page: where the pause bar shows, or, at a headless stop you [watch](#watch-live), through the
view, which the editor's own **Pick**, **Record** and **Assert** cannot do; else they show held, saying **Watch to
use**. **Mock a request** lists the page's fetch
and XHR requests, credentials hidden: the one you choose becomes a `page.route`. Under the test, the window says the
code went to the editor, with what to review in it, or why not.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/picker-runs.png" alt="The Runs window beside a shop page stopped before a click on Checkout: the test, a card saying where it stopped with the call and its place, its controls and code actions, then the image of the page">
  <figcaption>The Runs window, beside a test stopped at a breakpoint.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Watch a test {#watch-live}

**Watch**, on a worker's row, shows its test's page as it paints, running or stopped, the controls above the view at a
stop and the stopped worker scrolled into view, and **Pause and watch** pauses it too: [Watch a local test](./watch-running-test). An older reporter's row says to update it; with one newer than
0.61.0, its stops have their own **Watch**, which watches each stop alone and, left on, the worker's next ones.

The view fills the window's width under a red **Live** badge. Only the window that asked gets the frames
([what is sent](./watch-running-test#what-is-sent-and-kept)), and watching also pauses while the editor is out of
reach. Under the page, the window shows what pixels cannot ([in your own tools](./live-view-layers#in-your-own-tools)),
and **Open the trace so far**, in a watched page's head, opens Playwright's trace viewer on the running test's trace
up to now ([Open the trace so far](./watch-running-test#open-the-trace-so-far)).

At a headless stop, which nobody sees, the picker, the recorder's panel and the check panel appear in the watched
view, answered there as in a headed browser; their code reaches the editor the same way.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/picker-runs-live.png" width="488" alt="The Runs window at a headless stop, watching the shop page live: Watch and Interact pressed in the page card's head, the Live badge on the view, the picker over the page, with Resume, Step and Finish in one group, End the test apart, and Pick, Record, Assert and More under Code">
  <figcaption>A headless test's page watched live, with Pick started in it.</figcaption>
</figure>

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/picker-runs-ci.png" width="488" alt="The Runs window listing CI run #78 on main with its two running tests, each with Watch and Watch on the dashboard, the second watched: its page live under a Live badge, with the call it is at">
  <figcaption>A CI run's test, watched read-only.</figcaption>
</figure>

## Click and type on the view

While you watch, [**Interact**](./watch-running-test#interact), beside **Watch**, sends your pointer, wheel and keys
on the view to the page; a hint under the view says so the first time. Which reach the page, a paste included, and
which stay the window's: the [keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts#piwi-picker-s-runs-window).

## Pick on the image

**Pick on the image**, above the image, or a `Shift`+click on the image or the view, names the element a click
under the pointer would reach (a dialog or a banner over the page included), without touching the page: the locator
the pause bar's **Pick a locator** would rank first for it, sent to the editor in place of the stopped line's. The
window shows it, or why there is none, with **Copy** when no editor took it, on a headed stop's image too. `Esc` turns
it off. It needs Playwright 1.60 or later, and says so on an older one.

## The desktop app's runs

[Paired](./extension-connection#pair-with-the-desktop-app) with the [desktop app](./desktop), the window
lists the runs the app starts beside your editor's, marked **Desktop app**: reproductions, bisect steps and bug reports
included, with the same controls and **Watch**, and its failures to reach the app name the app (**Not connected to the
desktop app**). With no editor paired, it follows the app alone. The app holds no
editor, so its **Pick**, **Record** and **Assert** buttons are not offered; the code of **Assert a region**
and **Mock a request** goes to the app's window to copy, as the window here says: [Desktop app runs](./desktop-runs).

## Limits

- **The top frame.** Pick on the image refuses an element inside an iframe.
- **What a view shows.** A test's own screencast, a heavy page, a popup, a download and a dialog: [Watch a running
  test](./watch-running-test#limits).
- **The middle button stays the window's.** It would open a link in a tab the view does not show; `Shift`+click picks
  instead of clicking.

## Related

- [Pause and step from the editor](./editor-run-control): the controls and the paused line, in the editor.
- [Code from a pause](./editor-stop-code): what each action writes, and where.
- [Browser extension](./extension): Piwi Picker's other tools, and its permissions.

  on your machine alone.

# Desktop app

The desktop app runs the **entire dashboard on your machine**, with no Docker, `npx` or server to set up. It
bundles the Docker image's server in a native window and adds what only a local app can. Its runs:
[Local runs tray](./local-runs-tray) for each run, [Desktop app runs](./desktop-runs) for each worker.

## What it does

- **Receives your local runs** with no URL or token in your Playwright config.
- **Links a project to its folder**, so a run page can re-run the failed tests here.
- **Reproduces and bisects** a failure, or a flake, in a throwaway worktree, also for your editor.
- **Imports** a blob report or trace dropped on the window.
- **Connects AI assistants** to its MCP server by writing their config.

Everything binds to `127.0.0.1`.

## Where it is

- Piwi Desktop: The dashboard on your computer, with your local runs. On the [latest release](https://github.com/PiwiTests/piwi/releases/latest): Windows x64, per user (.exe): `Piwi-Desktop_x64-setup.exe`; Windows x64, per machine (.msi): `Piwi-Desktop_x64.msi`; macOS, Apple silicon (.dmg): `Piwi-Desktop_aarch64.dmg`; Linux x86-64, any distribution (.AppImage): `Piwi-Desktop_amd64.AppImage`; Debian, Ubuntu, x86-64 (.deb): `Piwi-Desktop_amd64.deb`; Fedora, RHEL, x86-64 (.rpm): `Piwi-Desktop_x86_64.rpm`.

What each installer needs:

| OS | Installer |
|----|-----------|
| **Windows** (x64) | `.exe` (per-user, no admin) or `.msi` (per-machine) |
| **macOS** 13.5+ (Apple silicon) | `.dmg` |
| **Linux** (x86-64) | `.AppImage`, `.deb` or `.rpm`, each needing a system WebKitGTK (`webkit2gtk-4.1`) |

The installers, [Piwi Runner](./piwi-runner)'s too, are **unsigned**: on macOS, open the app
once, then **Open Anyway** in **Privacy & Security**; on Windows, **More info** then **Run anyway** in SmartScreen.

Its data, and how to back it up: [the desktop app's data](/operate/backup-restore#the-desktop-app).

The tray menu, in the editors' order: **Show the stopped test** if one waits, **Open Piwi Desktop**, **Stop** per
running test (machine kept awake), **MCP server…**, **Desktop app settings…**, **Run in background** (off, closing
the window quits), **Start on login**, **Check for updates…**, **Open data folder**, **Show logs**, **Quit Piwi Desktop**. The windows open where you left them, with [keyboard shortcuts](/reference/keyboard-shortcuts#desktop-app)
and macOS menu items. **Open in a
window**, on a worker of the [Local runs tray](./desktop-runs), keeps it on top, then says how its run ended.
While a run reports into the app, from the app, an editor, a terminal or CI, its progress shows on the taskbar button or
the Dock icon and the window's title (`Running 3/9`), and a dot on the system tray icon (and the taskbar button, on Windows)
says how it stands: blue while it runs, red once a test failed, violet while a test of the app's runs, or of an
editor's, waits at a stop for you (`1 test waits for you`). A run from the window's Local runs tray flashes its outcome
as it ends (slate when interrupted), whatever else runs, and, failed while you look away, bounces the Dock icon or
flashes the taskbar button, a bisect or a lab only at its verdict; an editor's, a terminal's or CI's run, or one from
before a reload, never does. On Windows, the taskbar button's thumbnail has **Open**, which restores the window, and
**Stop**, which stops the window's run started last, the next one at a second click. In the background,
[notifications](/features/notifications#browser) arrive as OS notifications with no setup, plus an unread count on the
dock icon or system tray tooltip.

It listens on port 3000, or the one set in the `.exe` installer or in **Settings → Desktop app** (`serverPort` in
`settings.json`), a free one when taken.

## Sending results to it

While the app runs, the reporter finds it itself: a config with only a `projectName` reports here. It reads the
address and token the app writes to `~/.piwi/desktop.json` only when nothing else sets a server, so a CI job is never
redirected, and sends the token only to a server that proves it holds it
([details](/guide/reporter#finding-the-desktop-app-automatically)). A suite reporting to a shared dashboard sends its
local runs here with
[`desktopApp: 'prefer'`](/guide/reporter#local-runs-to-the-desktop-app-ci-to-a-team-server), which the
**Connect a suite** snippets carry with **CI reports to a team server** on.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/setup-connect-desktop.png" alt="The connect wizard in the desktop app: the one init command with no server URL, the fixtures import and the test command, and the CI reports to a team server switch, off">
  <figcaption>The desktop app's connect wizard: no URL to set.</figcaption>
</figure>

When the tests run as another user or in a container, **Settings → Desktop app** gives the
address and token to configure by hand. Keep the token in `PIWI_API_KEY`.

A dashboard link opened in your browser opens in the app, closing its tab. A `piwi://open/<page>` link opens its
page there, starting the app if needed (macOS: from Applications; Linux: after one run).

## Projects from local folders

A project's folder holds its Playwright config (a monorepo's subfolder, not its root).
**Projects → New project → Choose folder…** creates a project from one, named as it would report, and checks its
setup: `npx @piwitests/reporter init` there fixes what is missing. The link stays local, under
**Project → Settings → Local folder**, with its checks, **Unlink** and **Change**, which suggests folders and checks
your pick. Linking it offers to import its earlier runs; [Open in editor](/features/ide-integration) resolves source
links against it when no workspace root is set; and a clone serves its git history without an
[SCM credential](/guide/source-control#on-the-desktop-app).

## Running tests from the app

A run, an execution, a cluster or a test runs again here with the folder's own Playwright: its run button lists
**This computer** under **Where**, and says what one click runs, such as **Re-run 3 failed tests** or **Run this
test** (×20 until a failure, traced) on a test case. Its arrow, its options and its dialog:
[Run on this computer](./run-on-this-computer).

- **Runs keep going while you browse**, in the **Local runs** tray, each under what it runs; results come here, with
  **Compare with run #N**. A [bug report](/features/replay-a-bug-report#running-it-with-playwright)
  from Piwi Picker runs there too.
- **Watch, pause and step** each worker from the Local runs tray, running or stopped: [Desktop app
  runs](/features/desktop-runs). While it goes on, the run's own page shows the same (**On your machine**), with its
  **Stop**, [**Hold failures**](/features/watch-a-run#hold-failures) and output.

### Reproducing a failure and finding the breaking commit

A fix plan's [reproduce and bisect](/features/fix-plans#reproduce-and-bisect) recipe can run here **without touching
your checkout**:

- **Reproduce here** checks out the failing commit in a throwaway
  [`git worktree`](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-worktree), installs its dependencies (reusing yours on an
  unchanged lockfile outside a workspace) and any missing browser, and runs the failing test with that commit's own
  Playwright, [stopping in your editor](./desktop-runs#a-reproduction-in-your-editor) when one is open.
- **Find the breaking commit here** bisects between the last green commit and the failing one, with live progress and
  a **Stop** that kills the test and what it started, resets the bisect and removes the worktree. The first bad commit
  is linked to your SCM host and recorded on the failure cluster.

### Jobs from your editor

On a team instance's failure, the [editor extensions](/features/editor-failures#the-failures-view) offer
**Reproduce in the desktop app** and **Find the breaking commit in the desktop app**; on a flaky test, or a failure
whose test has an untested suspect, a [Flake Lab](/features/flake-lab#from-the-editor-and-the-failure-pages) run of
the team instance's plan. The window shows the commits, tests or arms and runs nothing until you start it. The editor
gets the verdict and can share it on the team instance with its own key, which the app never holds.

## Importing local files

Drop a Playwright blob report or trace (`.zip`) on the window, or open one with **Open with → Piwi Desktop**, and
pick the project: it imports as on the [import page](/guide/importing-runs), several traces forming one run. A
[`.piwibug`](/reference/bug-report-file) becomes a [bug report](./bug-reports).

## Connecting AI assistants

The app serves the [MCP server](/features/mcp) with local tools a hosted instance lacks:
`import_local_report` (a local `.zip` into a project), `read_local_source` (the file on disk now),
`apply_locator_fix` (a recommended locator fix applied to the file, previewed by default), and the
[run tools](./desktop-runs#for-agents) for the runs it starts. It registers as `piwi-desktop`, beside a hosted Piwi.

**Settings → MCP server** connects Claude Code, Cursor and other clients it detects in one click:
[the desktop app's client setup](/features/mcp#in-the-desktop-app).

## Updates

**Settings → About → Updates** checks for a newer release (also at startup), lists what changed since your version,
breaking changes first, and installs it on restart; the tray's **Check for updates…** installs and restarts.
The `.exe` needs no admin rights; the `.msi` does. Downloads are signature-checked.

## Limits

- **One machine, one user.** It accepts results only from this machine; a team needs the
  [Docker image](/operate/deployment).
- **Local runs need the checkout**: a linked folder (a monorepo's subfolder works) with Playwright installed, plus `git`
  and your package manager for reproduce, bisect (one repository) and the lab.
- **No public address**: no [pull-request feedback](/features/pr-feedback), [auto-heal](/features/auto-heal),
  [share links](/features/share-links) or Jira webhook; email only with SMTP set.

# Run on this computer

In the [desktop app](./desktop)'s window, the [run button](./ci-rerun#the-run-dialog) of a run, an execution, a
failure cluster and a test runs the page's tests in the project's linked folder, with the folder's own Playwright and
the app's bundled Node. Its dialog's **Where** lists **This computer** in place of your apps
([Run on my machine](./run-on-my-machine), which a browser offers), before the project's [CI actions](./ci-actions).
The run streams into the [Local runs tray](./local-runs-tray), keeps going while you browse, and, with the Piwi
reporter set up, reports to the app.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/run-on-this-computer.png" alt="The run dialog of a failed run in the desktop app: the failed tests, the flaky ones or every test under What; This computer picked under Where, in the linked folder, above a CI action; then the linked folder, the run options and the environment">
  <figcaption>A failed run's dialog in the desktop app, on This computer.</figcaption>
</figure>

## One click

The button says what it runs, and runs it here in one click:

| Page | The button | Its other tests here |
|---|---|---|
| Run | **Re-run 3 failed tests**, else the flaky ones, else every test | The flaky tests and every test, by their files past 200 tests |
| Execution | **Re-run this test** | None: every test of its cluster runs on CI |
| Test | **Run this test**, by its title, 20 times with a trace until it fails | None: Flake Lab runs from the **Flakiness** tab |
| Failure cluster, and its Verify section | **Re-run the 2 affected tests**, as the verify command selects them | None |
| A run's **Tests** tab, tests selected | **Re-run 3 selected tests**, on this computer alone | None |

It names what differs from Playwright's defaults, and the [environment](./environments) of the run its tests come from
(**· headed · ×5 · Staging**): the run is for that environment, with its [run variables](./run-variables). For a
protected environment, the button's run is for none, and the dialog picks it.

While a run of those tests goes on, the button shows how far it is (**Running 2/3…**), then **Passed** or **Failed**
for a few seconds; a click then opens the tray, and never stops anything.

After a send to a CI action, the button reads **Run on this computer or CI** and opens the dialog on that action, until
a run here makes This computer its **Where** again. The button remembers the last one per project.

## The arrow

- **Runs this command**: what the button runs, and the tests it leaves out, those with no file path Playwright takes,
  or no title when it selects them by title.
- **Run once** headless, headed, in the inspector or in UI mode, and **Run other tests**: the page's other tests.
- The one-click runs on CI, as in a browser.
- **Options of this button**: **Record trace**, [**Hold failures**](./watch-a-run#hold-failures), **Repeat each** with
  no retries, **Stop at the first failing repetition**, and **Select tests by** `file:line`, title or file. They apply
  to this button's runs until you leave the page; the project's defaults, which every button starts from, are in
  **Project → Settings → Local folder**.
- **Run with options…**, **Copy as command** (the command for your terminal, with the run variables),
  **Project defaults…**, **Local runs**, and the linked folder with **Change linked folder…**.

## The dialog

**Run with options…** opens the run dialog on This computer: **What**, **Where**, the linked folder with **Change**,
the run options with **Repeat each** up to 1,000, the environment, and the exact commands. The options start from the
button's and apply to that run alone. The environment starts on the last one picked for the folder; a protected one
asks you to confirm each run, which keeps to the tests carrying its required tags. **Run** starts the run and closes the dialog.

## When the folder is not ready

With no folder linked, none of the tests in it, or no Playwright installed, the button opens the dialog, which says
what to fix: **Choose folder…**, **Choose the right folder…** or **Re-check after installing**. A folder without the
tests still runs, since a config may put them elsewhere. The arrow lists the same fixes. With no test it can select,
the button opens the arrow, which says why.

## Limits

- **The desktop app only.** A browser has no This computer: its run button asks your own apps instead.
- **A run's tests, one test, a cluster's tests or a selection.** A project's whole suite, its tagged tests and a Flake
  Lab experiment run on CI from the run button; Flake Lab also runs here from a test's **Flakiness** tab.

- [Desktop app runs](./desktop-runs): each worker, paused, stepped and watched live.

# Desktop app runs

This page is about each worker of a run the [desktop app](./desktop) starts: its stops, its page and the code a stop
makes. Every Playwright run the app starts names the app as its hub: a **Re-run** of tests, a reproduction, a bisect
step, a [Flake Lab](./flake-lab) run and a bug report's run. Its **Local runs** tray shows each worker of the run
beside its output, and steers the test as the editor does: [Pause and step from the editor](./editor-run-control).
Nothing leaves your machine unless you [share a run live](#share-live). The tray's runs themselves, their progress,
**Stop**, **Run again**, their output and a reload: [Local runs tray](./local-runs-tray).

## Each worker

While a run goes on, the tray shows each worker's test, project and attempt, and whether it runs.
**Pause** stops the test before its next call that acts on or checks the page. A test also stops at a `page.pause()`,
and a headed one shows Piwi's [pause bar](./editor-breakpoints#pause-a-run) there.

At a stop, the tray says why the test stopped, the call about to run (**Next**) and its place in your code (**At**),
with an image of the page. **Resume** lets the test go on, **Step** runs one call and stops before the next, **Finish**
runs it to its end without stopping again, and [**End the test**](./end-the-test) skips the rest.

A run of several workers shows one at a time, behind a tab each (**worker 2**), with **Pause all** and **Resume all**,
as in the [Runs window](./runs-window#the-controls).

[**Hold failures**](./watch-a-run#hold-failures), a switch on each running run, holds a failing test at its line:
**Failed at**, its error under it, and **Resume** to let it end as it failed. It is on from the start for
**Reproduce**, which runs to show you the failure, and for a run started with it on; **Run again** keeps it. The
switch turns off as the app's last window closes, unless another tool set it since.

<figure>
  <img src="/screenshots/desktop-run-live.png" alt="The Local runs tray of the desktop app: a running run with its Hold failures switch, and its checkout test stopped at its page.pause() before its click on Pay now, its page watched live with Interact on, with Resume, Step, Finish, Assert a region and Mock a request">
  <figcaption>A run the desktop app started, stopped at a <code>page.pause()</code> and watched live.</figcaption>
</figure>

The tray opens at each stop, and tells you of one in the background:
[stops while you look elsewhere](./local-runs-tray#stops-while-you-look-elsewhere).

## Watch

**Watch**, on a running worker in the tray or its test on the run's page, shows its page as the test runs and at each
stop, until you turn it off ([Watch a local test](./watch-running-test)).

At a stop of a worker nobody watches, **Watch** shows the stopped page as it paints, in place of its image, and stays
on for the worker's next stops until you turn it off. [**Interact**](./watch-running-test#interact), beside it, plays
your input on the page; `Tab` leaves the view unless a click into it took the keyboard. Nothing keeps the [frames](./watch-running-test#what-is-sent-and-kept).

**Pause and watch**, on a running test of the run's page in the app (**Open run #N** on the run in the tray), pauses
the test as **Pause** does and watches its worker: the tray opens at the stop, the page live, and the row says where
it stopped, with **Show its page** to open the tray on it again.

**Pick on the image** (Playwright 1.60 or later), or a `Shift`+click on the image or the view, names the element under
the pointer: its locator shows under the test, with **Copy**.

Under a watched page, the tray shows what pixels cannot ([beside the image](./watch-running-test#beside-the-image)),
and **Open the trace so far**, in its head, opens Playwright's trace viewer on the running test's trace up to now
([Open the trace so far](./watch-running-test#open-the-trace-so-far)).

**Inspect**, beside it, shows that test's page at each call as [on the run page](./live-inspect), with the locator
picker. The app's server reads the trace file **Open the trace so far** checks, while the tray shows the lane and the
window is not hidden; the window hears each page's call and reads the page rendered, never the file's path. Each page
is cleaned as a worker cleans it for the run page, the values any frame's secret fields held hidden in every page,
iframes included, and stays in memory until the test ends. As Inspect opens, it reads a page's snapshots since its
navigation, 8,192 or 16 MB at most; every lane's pages, with the snapshots read to build them, share 256 MB, past
which it keeps no more. A page with a frame it cannot read whole shows again from its next navigation, and the reading
stops when the trace folder, a folder above it or its `resources` folder becomes a link or no longer a folder: Inspect
says why each time.

## Code to copy

The app holds no editor, so the code a stop makes (**Assert a region**, **Mock a request**, a picked locator) comes to
the tray, to copy: [Code from the runs](./local-runs-tray#code-from-the-runs).

## Share live

A run that reports to your team's Piwi instance can be [shared live](./share-live#from-the-desktop-app) there for a
teammate to watch: who sees what, and why a run cannot be. **Stop sharing…** asks first, naming what closes there.

## For agents

The app's [MCP server](./mcp) (its **MCP server** page connects your coding agent) serves these runs with
the tools of [Run control for agents](./agent-run-control): an agent follows a run, pauses or steps it, and reads and
acts on the stopped page as you can and [no further](./agent-run-control#what-keeps-it-safe).
Its `run_start` starts a run of the tray, titled with the agent's name
([in the desktop app](./agent-run-control#in-the-desktop-app)).

The tray shows what it does: a stop it asked for says so (**Paused by the agent**), as does its first action at a
stop. The code `code_write` makes (the steps it took, an assertion, or a locator for the stopped line) comes under
**Code from the runs**, to copy, and back to the agent in its answer. An agent sees no Flake Lab run, bisect or lab
job: nobody attends them.

The tray names who else is there: the tools that have a run open (**Also open in Piwi Picker · An agent follows this
run**), who watches a worker's page, and who [drives a stop](/guide/concepts#presence-driving-a-stop): **Take control**
from an agent, and **Give back**.

An agent pauses, steps or runs to a line only while the app's window is open, in the tray included: a headless stop
goes on with no window to show it. A stop it asked for goes on two minutes after its last call.

## A reproduction in your editor

A job the app runs in a throwaway worktree of a commit (**Reproduce here**, a bisect step, a [Flake Lab](./flake-lab)
run) follows the editor window whose workspace holds the project's linked folder, by the rules a
[terminal run follows](./terminal-runs#which-editor-or-the-desktop-app), else the app. It follows only an editor
extension that knows these reproductions (an older one leaves it to the app), and a bisect step or a Flake Lab run,
which nobody attends, only one that knows such runs too.

- **Its stops show in the editor** at the failing line of the worktree's file, outside the workspace, marked
  **the desktop app's reproduction at commit abc1234, in a throwaway checkout**. A reproduction holds its failures from
  its start, as in the app.
- **Its code is to copy.** Assert, Assert a region and Mock a request offer the code with **Copy the code** and write
  nothing: "This reproduction runs at commit abc1234 in a throwaway checkout: copy the code into your own file."
  Record is refused there, and a pick goes to the app's window, to copy.
- **The app keeps it.** Its Local runs tray says where its tests wait (**In Visual Studio Code**), read only, stops it,
  and shows its verdict when it ends; the editor offers no Stop.

## Limits

- **No recording.** **Record**, and a stopped test's **Pick** and **Assert** buttons, which act in the test's
  window, end in an editor: run the test
  from VS Code or a JetBrains IDE to use them.
- **A linked folder.** A reproduction or a bisect step runs in a throwaway worktree, which no project links: its
  stops make no code here. With an editor open on the linked folder, the job runs on that editor instead, which offers
  its code to copy ([A reproduction in your editor](#a-reproduction-in-your-editor)).
- **A file changed since the run started** makes no code: run the test again.
- **Run to the cursor** stays in the editor, which has the file.

## Related

- [Local runs tray](./local-runs-tray): the tray's runs, their progress, their output and the runs list.
- [Pause and step from the editor](./editor-run-control): the same stops, in VS Code and the JetBrains IDEs.
- [Code from a pause](./editor-stop-code): what each action writes.
- [Runs window](./runs-window#the-desktop-app-s-runs): Piwi Picker's window, paired with the app, for the same runs;
  the code it starts at their stops comes to this tray.
- [Run control for agents](./agent-run-control): the tools an agent steers the runs with.
- [Flake Lab](./flake-lab#in-the-desktop-app): **Reproduce this flake** and a flake-aware bisect, run by the app.
