# Gap detectors & exposure

The [detectors](/guide/concepts#detector) that turn the [Test Map](/features/scenario-gaps) into scenario gaps, the
**exposure** score that ranks them, and the rules that decide what the graph holds. Evidence counts use the last 30
runs of the project's default branch: never a pull-request run, a probe or Flake Lab run, a bisect step or a
reproduction, nor a run flagged as an environment incident. *Changed, unreached* reads the window of
[change coverage](/features/uncovered-changes#one-rule-for-every-changed-file) instead.

## Detectors

The Test Map is recomputed after every run of the default branch, nightly, and on demand (**Recompute** in the Coverage
tab's Gaps view), always for the default branch whatever branch ran last. Every detector reads the runs the
[capture fixtures](/guide/capture-fixtures) record; **Needs** names what else it reads, and a detector stays silent
without it.

| Detector | Class | Finds | Needs | Confidence | Example evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Success only**<br>`success-only` | blind-spot | a route observed at least five times, always with a 2xx or 3xx status: its error paths never ran | nothing more | observations ÷ 20, plus 0.3 when the route documents an error status; at most 1 | `Observed 412 times over the last 30 runs, always 200` |
| **Declared, never hit**<br>`declared-never-hit` | blind-spot | a route or page the application declares that no test reaches | a [declared surface](/features/scenario-gaps#declared-surface) | 0.7 | `Declared in OpenAPI · 0 tests in 30 runs · documents 200, 404` |
| **Surface drift**<br>`surface-drift` | blind-spot | a route, page, control, link, handler or dependency first seen in the latest run that no test reaches (a handler through the routes it serves, a dependency through the handlers that call it); never a feature, and nothing in the run that built the graph first | nothing more | 0.4 | `Appeared in run #830; no test reaches it yet` |
| **Control nobody exercises**<br>`control-nobody-exercises` | blind-spot | a control on a page that no test's locator targets | the page inventory and the [locator index](/features/locator-usage) | 0.3 plus 0.1 per page, at most 0.8 | `On 12 page(s) · no locator targets it` |
| **Reachable, unvisited**<br>`reachable-unvisited` | blind-spot | a page other pages link to that no test navigates to | the page inventory | 0.4 plus 0.1 per linking page, at most 0.8 | `Linked from 7 page(s) · never navigated to` |
| **Escaped defect**<br>`escaped-defect` | blind-spot | a page with [bug reports](/features/bug-reports) no test names yet, one gap per page | Piwi Picker sending reports | 0.6 plus 0.1 per further report, at most 1 | `Bug report #37: Coupon not applied to the total — no test names it yet` |
| **Fixed without a regression test**<br>`fixed-without-test` | blind-spot | a [bug report](/features/bug-reports) closed in the last 180 days while no test names it | Piwi Picker sending reports | 0.7 | `Bug report #2 was fixed without a regression test: Gift card balance shown twice` |
| **Changed, unreached**<br>`changed-unreached` | blind-spot | an [uncovered change](/features/uncovered-changes#one-rule-for-every-changed-file), at pull-request time: a changed file Piwi can observe that no test reached, in the run or the last 30, and no suite ran a changed line of | the [source control](/guide/source-control) diff: a token for a private repository | 0.9 | `+41 −3 · no test in run #812 or in the last 30 runs` |
| **New error path**<br>`new-error-path` | blind-spot | at pull-request time, an error status (400 to 599) the change makes a route's handler answer with or throw, which no run of the route answered with, this one included | the source control diff (a token for a private repository) and a pull request | 0.55 | `Adds 422 to POST /api/orders · never observed` |
| **New control**<br>`new-control` | blind-spot | at pull-request time, a button, field, select or switch the change adds to a page file, on a page a test reaches, named by its static label, placeholder, name or text | the source control diff (a token for a private repository) and a pull request | 0.5 | `Adds button "Apply promo" on /checkout` |
| **Intent without a test**<br>`intent-without-test` | blind-spot | at pull-request time, a pull request whose title's words (half of them at least) no test's title, describe path, tags or feature holds | the source control diff (a token for a private repository) and a pull request | 0.4 | `feat: apply a promo discount · no test title, tag or feature matches` |
| **Single covering test**<br>`single-covering-test` | fragile | a node exactly one trusted test reaches, or that only untrusted tests reach | nothing more | 0.5; 0.6 when only untrusted tests reach it | `Only checkout › coupon reaches this`; `Only toggles dark mode (flaky) reaches this` |
| **Orphan test**<br>`orphan-test` | fragile | a test whose every reached node went unseen through the default branch's last 30 complete runs | nothing more | 0.4 | `All 3 node(s) it reaches disappeared from recent runs` |
| **Fix did not hold**<br>`fix-did-not-hold` | fragile | a failure cluster whose fix later regressed | nothing more | 0.6 | `Fixed in a1b2c3d · regressed 6 days later` |
| **Incidental catch**<br>`incidental-catch` | fragile | a failure cluster whose recorded fix changed one to three files, no test file among them, that none of the tests it failed is about by name or reaches | [source control](/guide/source-control) | 0.45 | `src/pricing/rounding.ts is caught only incidentally` |
| **Not noticed**<br>`not-noticed` | false-comfort | a route a probe broke while no test noticed (a delay never counts) | [probes](/features/probes) | 0.8 | `A probe (status-500) on POST /api/orders did not make checkout › pay fail` |
| **Passed with errors**<br>`passed-with-errors` | false-comfort | a test whose newest execution in the default branch's last 30 runs passed while the application reported an error: a 5xx from one of its routes, a backend log at error level, or a console error or uncaught page error from its own origin | nothing more; backend logs need the [instrumentation](/guide/backend-logs) | 0.6 | `Passed · run #73 · the backend logged an error on PATCH /api/orgs/current` |
| **Assertion-light**<br>`assertion-light` | false-comfort | a page some test asserts on, every check there only that an element is visible, hidden, attached or in the viewport | the locator index | 0.4 | `2 tests assert on this page, only that elements are present` |
| **Catalog method, no test calls**<br>`catalog-method-no-test-calls` | blind-spot | a page-object method or helper on a reached page that no test runs | the [test functions catalog](/features/test-functions) | 0.5 | `./pages/UsersPage · goToNextPage · page reached by 3, called by 0` |
| **Code nobody executes**<br>`code-not-executed` | blind-spot | the functions of a file no suite ran in the default branch's newest [combined coverage](/features/combined-coverage), or a file recorded by line none of whose lines ran; the 30 files with the most, one gap each | a coverage report or run coverage | 0.4 plus 0.3 times the share of its functions not run; 0.6 for a whole file | `Functions at lines 12–20, 22–30 · no suite ran them at 9a8b7c6` |
| **Single covering function**<br>`single-covering-function` | fragile | the functions of a file exactly one test runs in the tests' latest coverage on the default branch, [quarantined tests](/features/flaky-tests#quarantine-with-a-way-out) left out, or that only quarantined tests run; the 30 files with the most, one gap each | per-test [code reach](/features/code-reach) | 0.5 | `Only checkout pays runs the functions at lines 7–9` |
| **Error path never executed**<br>`error-path-not-executed` | blind-spot | a `catch` block, a `throw`, or a statement answering with an error status (`TypedResults.NotFound()`, `res.status(409)`) that no suite ran, inside a function that ran (inside a file that ran, when the coverage records it by line): the code-level form of *Success only*. The 30 files that ran with the most lines not run, read at the commit's version | a coverage report or run coverage, and the [source control](/guide/source-control) connection to read the files | 0.7 | `Line 59 · return TypedResults.NotFound(); · its function ran, this never did` |
| **Unprobed dependency**<br>`unprobed-dependency` | false-comfort | a dependency a route's handler calls that no probe has decided | server spans | 0.3 plus 0.1 per calling route, at most 0.7 | `Called by 4 route(s) · no probe has checked what happens when it fails` |
| **Not handled**<br>`not-handled` | unhandled, degraded | the application did not cope with a server probe's fault; a finding, not a gap | [server probes](/features/probes#server-probes) | 1 unhandled, 0.5 degraded | `A server probe made POST /api/orders fail; the application did not handle it` |

*Error path never executed* scans brace-syntax source (TypeScript, JavaScript, C#, Java): a comment line is skipped,
and a brace inside a string can end a `catch` block early. It runs on **Recompute** and the nightly sweep, which read
the files through the source control connection; a file the provider cannot serve keeps its gap as it was.

*Passed with errors* leaves out a console line or an uncaught error from another origin's script and the browser's own
*Failed to load resource* line. A response no server sent, such as one the test's route handler fulfilled, is no 5xx of
the application, and a test that fulfills a failing response means to see the page fail, so its page's errors do not
count either.
*Assertion-light* counts any other matcher (a text, a count, a value, an attribute) as a value check, and so is a read
of an element the index cannot name, or a visible element found by a text holding a number
(`getByText('Total: $42.00')`); an `expect` on no locator, such as a downloaded file's name, never reaches the index,
so a page checked only that way reads as light. A test calls a catalog method when one of its default-branch
locator uses does what one of the method's steps does, on the element that step names by test id or name, on a page
its URL pattern matches. A method whose every target comes from a parameter gets no decision.

A trusted test is judged on the default branch's last 30 runs: it did not pass only after a retry in any of them, did
not flip between failing and passing three times across them, did not fail each of its last three, is not quarantined, and was neither skipped nor left unrun in the newest it ran in.
A test with no run among them stays trusted. *Surface drift* raises a node in the run it first appears in; a node
only untrusted tests reach is then a *Single covering test* gap. *Changed, unreached* is covered on
[Uncovered changes in pull requests](/features/uncovered-changes). When each gap closes:
[When a gap closes](#when-a-gap-closes).

Runs record reach to routes and pages: a test reaches every route its page requested, every page it ran a locator
call on, and the page it ended on. Each recompute adds reach to controls and links from the default branch's
[locator index](/features/locator-usage), for uses seen in the last 180 days. A test reaches a control when one of its
locators names it by role and name, when an alternative captured for that locator does, or when the name matches as
Playwright matches it without `exact` (a case-insensitive part of exactly one name of that role). A label,
placeholder or title reaches the one input-like control (textbox, combobox, checkbox, radio, switch, …) carrying that
name. Triage adds reach too (*covered by* or *covered elsewhere*), but *Control nobody exercises* stays silent until a
locator reaches some control on the project. A test that clicks or fills an element no node matches, through a test
id or a CSS selector, might have used any control on that page, so *Control nobody exercises*, *Single covering
test* and *Surface drift* raise none of those controls.

## When a gap closes

Gaps persist across recomputes, so triage survives them. A gap **closes itself** when its detector no longer raises
it, for example once its node gains a trusted test, and a closed gap the detector raises again reopens. Beyond that
rule:

- **Covered by** closes a gap and records the covering test as reaching the node; such a gap stays closed when its
  detector raises it again. A dismissed gap keeps its verdict.
- **Surface drift** stays open until any test reaches the node or the node leaves the graph, unless you dismiss it or
  close it with *Covered by* first.
- **Changed, unreached** closes when a later diff no longer counts its file as uncovered, or when the next recompute
  finds the file reached, out of the coverage scope, deleted or no longer observable. An accepted one closes only once
  a test reaches the file. A file no later diff reads, such as the old path of a rename or a file of an abandoned pull
  request, keeps its gap until a test reaches it or it is triaged.
- **The pull-request detectors** (*New error path*, *New control*, *Intent without a test*) close when a later run of
  the pull request no longer raises them.
- **Not noticed** closes once a probe of its route is noticed.
- **A finding** (*Not handled*) never closes itself: triage it.

A closed gap keeps why it closed: [Close reasons and acted on](#close-reasons-and-acted-on).

## Exposure

A gap's score is its detector's confidence (the table above) times its **exposure**, the geometric mean of four factors. Each factor is
kept between 0.1 and 1, so a missing input lowers the score without zeroing it.

| Factor | From | Reaches 1 at |
|---|---|---|
| **Churn** | commits touching the files: on a pull request, among the base branch's newest twelve in the last 90 days | 12 commits |
| **Age** | on a pull request, the days since the oldest of those commits; older weighs more, since escaped defects concentrate there. The 90-day scan stops it near 0.25 | one year |
| **Escape history** | whether a file was part of a failure cluster's fixing commit, or a bug report from the last 180 days names the gap's page (the page holding its control) | yes, else 0.1 |
| **Priority** | the highest [`piwi:priority`](/reference/test-metadata#ownership-metadata-piwi-annotations) of the tests reaching the node: critical 1, high 0.7, medium 0.4, low 0.2 | critical |

Churn, age and escape history come from the [source control](/guide/source-control) connection and apply to the
files a pull request changed. A gap on a route, a handler or a dependency draws churn and escape history from the
handler files behind it, and a gap on a file's code from that file, read from the diffs default-branch runs recorded over the last 90 days. Each run diffs from
its [last green run](/features/run-changes#the-baseline), so churn counts distinct diffs, and the runs of a red streak count once. Escape history marks the
files in the diff that ended on a fixing commit, which holds every change since the last green run. Age needs each
file's history, so it stays at 0.1 there. The other detectors
rank by priority and confidence. A finding ranks by its severity (1 for unhandled, 0.5 for degraded) times the
route's reach.

## Precision

Each verdict on a gap counts for or against its detector, on that project:

- **For**: accepted at any point, or closed with **Covered by**, even once the gap later closes, unless it was then
  dismissed as *wrong* or *covered elsewhere*.
- **Against**: dismissed as *wrong*, or as *covered elsewhere* (no test was missing). On a finding, *covered
  elsewhere* counts for neither.
- **Neither**: dismissed as *not worth testing*, or with no reason, and never accepted.

A detector's precision is its share of verdicts *for*. Below 60%, on a project with twenty or more verdicts, the
detector [mutes itself](/features/scenario-gaps#triage) there: its rows leave the pull-request comment, the Gaps digest,
the feature map and graph, its gaps sort last in the Gaps view and in the MCP tools, and the Gaps view and
**Settings → About** say so.

### Close reasons and acted on

A closed gap keeps why it closed, shown after its status in the Gaps view:

| Reason | Closed when |
|---|---|
| Acted on in its pull request | A run of the pull request that raised it answered it: reached its changed file, answered with its new status, or a test names its intent |
| A test reached it | A test reached its changed file, outside the pull request that raised it |
| No longer detected | Its detector no longer raises it |
| Covered by a test | Someone closed it with **Covered by** |
| Merged into another gap | Its subject merged into another one's |
| Detector retired | Its detector no longer runs |
| Out of the coverage scope, file deleted, not observable | The [change coverage](/features/uncovered-changes) read of its file |

Beside each detector's precision, Settings › About counts the gaps it raised on a pull request and how many that pull
request acted on. No one triages that number: it says how often a gap led to a test before the change merged.

## Features

A feature groups the routes, pages and controls the tests tagged with it reach. Each recompute also gives it what no
feature reaches, with a confidence below one: the controls on its pages (0.8), the pages they link to under the same
first path segment (0.6) and those pages' controls (0.5), and the declared routes under the same resource path as a
route it reaches, `/api/v1/orders` for `GET /api/v1/orders/:id` (0.6). A gap sits under one feature: the one whose
tests reach its node, else the most confident inference. A gap on a test sits under the test's feature, and one on a
catalog method under the feature owning most of the pages its URL pattern matches. So the map shows what a feature
misses, not only what its tests touch. Dependencies, links, and pages or declared routes under other paths stay
ungrouped.

With three features or more, a node more than half the tests reach, or that more than half the features and three at
least group, is a **hub**, such as the session route nearly every test calls. The feature graph still draws it, but
it adds no member, test, gap or link to a feature; its gaps sit under *Shared by most features*. The groups are rebuilt
on every recompute, so a feature that loses its tag leaves the map.

## What the graph includes

The graph stays proportional to the application's surface, not its data volume:

- **Your own origin only.** Route nodes come from requests to the Playwright `baseURL` of the run's projects (or the
  project's configured route origins); analytics beacons and CDN assets never become nodes.
- **A page load reaches its route.** A page load (`page.goto`, a link followed) reaches the route of its URL, so a
  route a backend serves by navigation is reached. *Success only* counts only the calls a page makes, a form's POST
  included, so a page never reads as a route without its error path.
- **Pages are path patterns.** A page's [page key](/guide/concepts#page-key) is its URL reduced to its path:
  `/orders/123` and `/orders/456` are one node, as is the same path from staging and production. Numbers, UUIDs,
  ULIDs, JWTs and long tokens become `:id`, `:uuid`, `:ulid`, `:jwt` and `:token`, and the host, query and hash are
  dropped; other ids (a Mongo ObjectId, a cuid, a slug) stay in the key, one node per value. A single-page app routed
  by the URL hash (`/#/settings`) is one page, `/`. The page each locator was used on and Piwi Picker's **This page**
  use the same key, where a page of another site keeps its origin in front of the path.
- **Routes drop the query.** `GET /api/orders?page=2` and `GET /api/orders?status=open` are one node, `GET /api/orders`.
- **Controls and links are templated.** Dates, ids and numbers in an accessible name become placeholders, and each
  page keeps at most 200 controls and 200 links. The page inventory reads a page as its URL changes, once per page
  per worker, so a control that renders later, or only in a dialog, is not in it; it records names and links, never
  a field value.
- **Branches stay separate.** A default-branch run writes the canonical graph; any other branch writes rows tagged
  with it, so a route added on a pull request never shows as drift on the default branch. Those rows drop when the
  pull request closes, or after 30 days unseen. Detectors read the canonical graph and the default branch's runs;
  change coverage reads every branch.
- **Old nodes retire.** A node unseen for 30 complete default-branch runs leaves the graph, unless an open, snoozed
  or accepted gap other than *Surface drift* is about it: that node stays until the gap is closed or dismissed, and a
  *Surface drift* gap closes with its node. With a [retention period](/operate/storage#data-retention), a node goes
  with the runs that saw it, whatever gap is about it.

# Test search

A run's **Tests** tab and a project's **Tests** tab share one search box and one language: words that look in every
text of a test, and qualifiers in the style of GitHub search that look in one field, such as `file:cart.spec.ts` or
`describe:"Guest checkout"`. The box lists the qualifiers when it is empty and the values each one can take as you type,
and the list marks what matched. `Ctrl` + `F` (`⌘` + `F` on macOS) jumps to the box; pressed again there, it opens the
browser's own find.

## Words and phrases

A word matches the test title, its describe blocks or its file path, and, on a run's Tests tab, the error text too.
Every word must match, in any of them: `login timeout` finds the tests that mention both. Quotes keep spaces inside one
term: `"guest checkout"`.

## Qualifiers

| Qualifier | Also written | Matches | Tests tab |
|---|---|---|---|
| `file:` | `path:` | The spec file path | Run and project |
| `describe:` | `suite:` | A describe block | Run and project |
| `title:` | `test:`, `name:` | The test title | Run and project |
| `tag:` | | A tag, with or without its `@` | Run and project |
| `browser:` | `project:` | The Playwright project the execution ran in | Run |
| `error:` | | The error text | Run |
| `lock:` | | A [lock](/reference/test-metadata#test-locks) the test declares | Run and project |
| `owner:` | | The `piwi:owner` [annotation](/reference/test-metadata#ownership-metadata-piwi-annotations) | Run and project |
| `priority:` | | The `piwi:priority` annotation | Run and project |
| `feature:` | | The `piwi:feature` annotation | Run and project |
| `id:` | | The test's [external ID](/reference/test-metadata#external-test-ids) | Run and project |
| `is:` | | `is:stuck`: a running test marked [Stuck?](/features/stuck-tests), while the run is live | Run |
| `worker:` | | The [worker lane](/reference/test-metadata#worker-lanes) the execution ran on, from 1 in each shard; a result from a reporter that sends no lane matches none | Run |
| `shard:` | | The shard the execution ran in, from 1 | Run |

How the terms combine:

- `file:`, `describe:`, `title:` and `error:` match anywhere in the text, and `*` stands for any characters:
  `file:checkout/*.spec.ts`. The other qualifiers match a whole value.
- Case and accents never matter: `resume` finds `Résumé`, and `CAFÉ` finds `cafe`.
- Every term must match. The exception is a qualifier of which a test has only one value (`file:`, `browser:`, `owner:`,
  `priority:`, `feature:`, `id:`, `worker:`, `shard:`): repeated, it matches any of the values, so
  `file:cart file:checkout` lists both files and `shard:1 shard:2` the first two shards.
- `is:stuck` reads what the dashboard knows of a running test while the run is live: on a run that has ended, it finds
  nothing.
- A leading `-` excludes: `-tag:slow`, `-describe:legacy`, `-flaky`.
- A qualifier the tab does not have, such as `error:` on a project, is read as a word.

## Examples

| Search | Finds |
|---|---|
| `file:cart` | The tests of every file whose path contains `cart` |
| `describe:"Guest checkout" -tag:slow` | The tests inside a *Guest checkout* block that are not tagged `@slow` |
| `timeout browser:webkit` | On a run: the WebKit executions whose title, blocks, path or error mention `timeout` |
| `owner:@team/payments priority:critical` | The critical tests the payments team owns |
| `title:"refund*email"` | The tests whose title has `refund`, then `email` further on |
| `is:stuck shard:2` | On a live run: the running tests of shard 2 that have run far longer than they usually do |
| `worker:3 -tag:slow` | On a run: what worker 3 ran, its `@slow` tests left out |

## Completion

The suggestions follow the term under the caret. An empty term lists the qualifiers; a qualifier lists the values it can
take, with how many tests carry each; a word lists the qualifiers it starts and the values that contain it. On a run the
values come from its executions; on a project, from every test case in the chosen age window.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `↓` / `↑` | Move through the suggestions |
| `Enter` / `Tab` | Take the highlighted suggestion |
| `Esc` | Close the suggestions |

While you type a qualifier's value, the closest match is highlighted, so `Enter` completes it. A plain word is never
replaced by a qualifier unless you move to one first.

## Order

Both tabs read in the order of the suite unless you pick another sort. A run's Tests tab opens in **Run order**, when
each test first started (a retried test counts from its first attempt), and in **File order** when grouped by file:
file path, then the line and column the test is declared at, the order `playwright test --list` prints. A project's Tests
tab opens in File order. In the *File + Describe* grouping, a describe block keeps its place in the file among the tests
around it. Outside that grouping, a test's describe blocks are named before its title: `Checkout › pays by card`.

The test catalog's `q` API parameter and the `query` argument of the MCP `get_project_test_catalog` tool take the same
language ([API docs](https://piwitests.dev/demo/settings/api), [MCP tools](/reference/mcp-tools)).

## Piwi Picker's Runs window

In [Piwi Picker's Runs window](/features/runs-window), for the stopped test whose row holds the focus, else the only
stopped test shown: a run's worker tabs show one worker at a time. Step and Finish wait for a stop that is no failure.

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| `F8` or `F5` | Resume |
| `F10` | Step |
| `Shift` + `F11` | Finish |

While **Interact** is on at a [watched stop](/features/runs-window#click-and-type-on-the-view), the view takes your
pointer: moves, left and right clicks, double and triple clicks as your system counts them, drags, and the wheel once
the view has the focus, with `Ctrl`, `Alt` and `⌘` held with a click held in the page too. It takes your keys while it
has the focus (a focus ring around it), and a paste, which types the clipboard's text: characters are typed, named keys (Enter, the arrows, Backspace, Delete, Home, End) pressed, with Shift, and
`Ctrl` (`⌘` on macOS) with A, Z, Y, Enter and the editing keys. The browser's other shortcuts, the function keys and
`Esc` stay the window's: `Esc` turns **Interact** off, gives
the stop back and moves the focus to **Interact**. While a pick or a check runs on the page, `Esc` goes to the page
instead, as its own key. `Tab` moves the focus on past the view, unless you clicked into
it: then `Tab` and `Shift+Tab` go to the page too, until `Esc` turns **Interact** off. Characters an input method composes (Chinese,
Japanese, Korean) do not reach the page; paste them instead. The desktop app's Local runs tray takes the same keys.
On a run's worker tabs, the arrow keys, `Home` and `End` move between the workers.

## The run shortcut

Piwi Picker's run shortcut works from any window. It resumes the stopped tests, else pauses every run, but a run
[nobody attends](/guide/concepts#hold-failures); Piwi Picker's toolbar icon shows what it did for a moment. It has no
key until you set one: **Set a shortcut**, in the Runs window, opens the browser's shortcuts page, where you give it a
key and, in Chrome and Edge, the **Global** scope. In Firefox, it works while Firefox has the focus.

# Editor commands

Every command the two editors offer, by what it acts on. VS Code lists them in the command palette under **Piwi:**;
a JetBrains IDE lists them under **Tools → Piwi**, a run's in its **Run control** submenu, and in
**Find Action**, says caret for cursor and project for window,
and shows a toggle's state with a check mark. A row that names one editor is that editor's alone. Some commands have a
shortcut in both editors ([Keys](#keys)); a run's controls take the debugger's keys
([The controls](/features/editor-run-control#the-controls)).

### Keys

`Ctrl+Shift+Alt` with a letter, `Cmd` for `Ctrl` on macOS. Record here… and Run the test at the cursor act in an editor
of a JavaScript or TypeScript file, the others there and in Piwi's views (the Piwi tool window in a JetBrains IDE), and
nowhere else. A JetBrains keymap where that chord is another action's in those places takes the letter of its row, as do
the keymaps descending from it. **Settings → Keymap** shows `$default` as Windows, `Mac OS X 10.5+` as macOS, `Mac OS X`
as IntelliJ IDEA Classic, and `Default for XWin`, `Default for GNOME` and `Default for KDE` as XWin, GNOME and KDE; it
drops ` OSX` and ` (Mac OS X)` from the other names, adding (macOS) on Windows and Linux.

| Keymap | Record here…, Stop recording | Re-run the failing tests | Run the test at the cursor | Open the failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VS Code, and `$default` and every JetBrains keymap not below | `R` | `F` | `K` | `B` |
| `Default for XWin`, `Default for GNOME`, `Default for KDE` | `R` | `F` | `K` | `G` |
| `Mac OS X 10.5+`, `Eclipse (Mac OS X)`, `Sublime Text (Mac OS X)`, `VSCode OSX`, `macOS System Shortcuts` | `Z` | `F` | `K` | `B` |
| `Visual Studio`, `Visual Studio 2022`, `Visual Assist` | `G` | `F` | `J` | `B` |
| `ReSharper` | none | `T` | `J` | none |
| `Visual Studio OSX`, `Visual Assist OSX` | `Z` | `F` | `J` | `B` |
| `ReSharper OSX` | `Z` | `T` | `J` | `S` |
| `TextMate` | `R` | `J` | `K` | `B` |

They share a key only with an action of the Database tool window or a database console's results, or of a Java, Kotlin
script, Go or Terraform file. **Preferences: Open Keyboard Shortcuts** changes them in VS Code (search `piwi`),
**Settings → Keymap** in a JetBrains IDE (search `Piwi`).

## Connection

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| **Piwi: Connect…**, **Piwi: Disconnect** | Choose the desktop app or an instance and its project, or forget them: [Editor connection](/features/editor-connection) |
| **Piwi: Open settings** | Piwi's settings: the instance and the project |
| **Piwi: Read the instance and the configs again** | Fetch the indexes and the latest run again and read the Playwright configs; in a JetBrains IDE, search the project for configs again and start a stopped editor service |
| **Piwi: Restart the editor service** | Stop the editor service and start it again |
| **Piwi: Open the log** | The editor service's log: its starts and ends, its errors and the requests that failed |
| **Piwi: Open the Piwi menu** | VS Code: the status bar item's menu, which a JetBrains IDE opens with a click on its item: [The editor's status bar](/features/editor-status-bar) |
| **Piwi: Node.js settings…** | JetBrains: choose the Node.js the editor service starts with |
| **Piwi: Get started** | Open the first steps: VS Code's walkthrough, or the Get started tab of the Piwi tool window in a JetBrains IDE |
| **Piwi: Open the documentation** | Open this site in the browser: [Editor extensions](/features/editors) from VS Code, [JetBrains plugin](/features/jetbrains) from a JetBrains IDE |

### Where the run controls are

- **In VS Code**: the Piwi item's menu while they apply, after **Go to the stopped line**; the command palette; the
  editor title, Pause or Resume, Step, Finish and Stop (on a run this window started) in the debug toolbar's order, the
  others under `…`; and, while a test is stopped, in the editor's context menu, right after its Go to entries, and on
  its worker's page (Resume, Step, Finish and Write code…).
- **In a JetBrains IDE**: **Tools → Piwi → Run control** and the **Run** menu, enabled while they apply; the toolbar of the run's
  Run tab, acting on that run; the status bar item's menu; and, while a test is stopped, first in the editor's context
  menu, and on its worker's tab (Resume, Step, Finish and Write code…).

A run is named after what it runs (`checkout.spec.ts:12`, `a.spec.ts and 2 more`, the title it greps, `×3` after a
Verify ×3, a Flake Lab line's command), in its terminal or Run tab and wherever you pick it, where it also has its
number on the instance once it has one (`Run #78 · checkout.spec.ts:12`). Two runs of one name show their refs.

# Editor settings

Both editors group their options as this page does: VS Code in its settings editor (search `piwi.`), and
**Settings → Tools → Piwi** in a JetBrains IDE, whose help button and **Documentation** links open this page. A row that
names one editor is that editor's alone; the JetBrains page has no Advanced group, and opens with the connection in use
and a group for the desktop app.

Each option is one of three kinds:

- **The team's**: one value for everyone on the project. VS Code reads it from the user or the workspace settings,
  which a repository may commit (`.vscode/settings.json`); a JetBrains IDE keeps it in `.idea/piwi.xml`, which the team
  can share.
- **Yours, which a project may set**: your choice, which a workspace's settings can set for that project. A JetBrains IDE
  keeps it for you in the project's `.idea/workspace.xml`.
- **Yours**: the same in every project. VS Code reads it from the user settings alone, so a repository cannot change it;
  a JetBrains IDE keeps it in the IDE's own settings (`options/piwi.xml`).

In Rider, a project's `.idea` files sit under `.idea/.idea.<Name>/.idea/`, as the settings page says.

## Connection

| Setting | What it chooses | Default | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| `piwi.serverUrl` | The Piwi instance. `PIWI_DASHBOARD_URL` in the environment or the workspace `.env` comes first, then this, then the desktop app while it runs: [Editor connection](/features/editor-connection) | none | The team's |
| `piwi.project` | The project's name or id on the instance | none | The team's |
| JetBrains: **Read this project from the desktop app while it runs** | Whether the desktop app comes first while it runs; VS Code chooses it with **Piwi: Connect…** | off | Yours, which a project may set |
| JetBrains: **Desktop app project** | The project's name in the desktop app; empty uses the one linked there to this folder | none | Yours, which a project may set |

The API key is kept in the editor's secret storage (VS Code) or the IDE's password safe, for its instance alone, and
the choice of the desktop app on this machine only.

## Runs

| Setting | What it chooses | Default | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| `piwi.runNotifications` | When a run ends, whether a notification says what it changed: always, only when something fails, or never | Say what it changed when something fails | Yours |
| `piwi.runNotificationsScope` | The runs it says it for: the runs started here, or also the branch's CI runs | The runs started here and the branch's CI runs | Yours |
| `piwi.statusBarAlert` | When the status bar item turns red: for a new failure a run started here caused, for any failing test, or never | For a new failure a run started here caused | Yours |
| `piwi.breakpoints` | Which runs pause at the editor's breakpoints, Debug with Piwi, every run or none: [Editor breakpoints](/features/editor-breakpoints) | Debug with Piwi | Yours |
| `piwi.runHeaded` | Whether every run Piwi starts runs headed, its browser window shown | off | Yours |
| `piwi.runHoldFailures` | [Hold failures](/features/watch-a-run) from each run's start: Auto, On or Off | Auto | Yours |
| `piwi.testExplorer` | VS Code: whether the Testing view lists Piwi's tests, with their results; off leaves the view to another extension's tree, such as Microsoft's Playwright Test | on | Yours, which a project may set |
| JetBrains: **Run the tests in the IDE's Playwright runner** | Whether a run starts in the IDE's Playwright runner (a test tree, Debug, Rerun Failed Tests) or in the Run tool window's console. The runner comes with the IDE's JavaScript plugin, as in WebStorm, IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate and Rider; where it lacks one, the option is off and says why | off | Yours |

## In the editor

| Setting | What it chooses | Default | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| `piwi.codeLens` | The lines Piwi writes above the code: every line, a failure's and an uncovered change's alone, or none. A test's gutter mark stays | Every line | Yours |
| `piwi.gutterIcons` | VS Code: each test's latest result in the gutter; off, its line keeps the hover. A JetBrains IDE switches it under **Settings → Editor → General → Gutter Icons → Piwi test results** | on | Yours |
| `piwi.coverageMarks` | The coverage marks at the left of the lines: [Editor coverage](/features/editor-coverage) | on | Yours |
| `piwi.failureSeverity` | How a failure shows at its line: an error, a warning, information (a weak warning in a JetBrains IDE), or nothing in the problems | An error | Yours, which a project may set |
| `piwi.locatorWarnings` | Whether a locator the [locator stability rules](/reference/locator-stability) find brittle is warned at, with its stable alternative as a quick fix | on | Yours |
| `piwi.failingTestTint` | Whether a failing test and the line it failed at are tinted; the gutter still marks them, unless `piwi.gutterIcons` is off | on | Yours |
| `piwi.ciPositions` | Whether a CI run of the branch shows where it stands, at the end of each line: [Editor CI runs](/features/editor-ci-runs) | on | Yours |
| `piwi.runningLines` | Which lines of your run are marked as running: every running test's, the watched worker's alone, or none: [The running line](/features/watch-running-test#the-running-line) | Every running test's | Yours |

## Agents (MCP)

| Setting | What it chooses | Default | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| `piwi.mcpAuthorization` | How the agent signs in to Piwi's MCP server: with the editor's API key, or a sign-in in the browser | The editor's API key | Yours |
| `piwi.serveRunsToAgents` | Whether the test runs started here are served to the agents of this machine, as an MCP server on `127.0.0.1` | on | Yours, which a project may set |

## Advanced

| Setting | What it chooses | Default | Kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| `piwi.hiddenMessages` | VS Code: the kinds of messages **Don't Show Again** hid: `agent-let-go` (a stop an agent held goes on once the agent went idle), `window-shared` (a run is shared live, as the window's runs are), `unattended-resumed` (a test stopped where nobody attends the run goes on), `reporter-missing` (a run did not reach the instance, from a config without the Piwi reporter) and `picker-inserted` (what Piwi Picker inserted at the cursor). Remove a kind to see its message again | none | Yours |
| `piwi.trace.server` | VS Code: whether the traffic with the editor service is traced in the Piwi output channel | Off | Yours |

# Notification events & webhooks

A [subscription](/features/notifications#subscriptions) picks one or more of these events. This page lists when each
one fires and what a webhook channel receives; channels, subscriptions and delivery are on
[Notifications & alerts](/features/notifications). Some runs fire none of them: a run from an editor, a Flake Lab or
probe run, a partial run from a developer's machine, and the others
[that send nothing](/reference/test-metadata#run-origin). A run flagged as an environment incident fires
`environment.incident` in place of the events its row names.

## Events

| Event | Fires when |
|-------|------------|
| `run.finished` | A run completes (any status) |
| `run.failed` | A run completes with failures, or stops at Playwright's global timeout (`status: "timedout"`) |
| `run.failed.default_branch` | A run fails, as `run.failed` reads it, on the repository's default branch |
| `run.interrupted` | A run stops reporting before its end and the stale-run sweep marks it interrupted (two minutes without activity, an hour for a run still in its global setup or with a shard still in its own, and an hour for a sharded run waiting for a shard that has not started, once every shard that started has ended; each counted at the earliest from when the server could be reached again, after a restart or a database outage). The payload is a run event's, with `status: "interrupted"` and the results stored so far; Flake Lab and probe runs send none |
| `cluster.new` | A new failure cluster appears in a run that ran to its end (passed, failed or timed out). A cluster first seen by a run that sent no notification of it (a run from an editor, a partial run from a developer's machine, an import, a cancelled or interrupted run) is announced by the first such run that sends notifications, unless the cluster is resolved, ignored or snoozed when that run ends, or its first run was deleted. When runs overlap, the first to end announces it and no other run does, whether or not a channel is subscribed |
| `cluster.fixed` | A run passes every test a cluster covers: the fix landed (a filtered re-run of just those tests counts). The payload's `verification` says whether the diagnosis was corroborated (`diagnosis-verified`) or the tests merely stopped failing, and `resolved` whether the triage status was closed automatically |
| `cluster.regressed` | A cluster with a recorded fix fails again, or one resolved by hand fails in a run started after it was resolved (no `fixLandedRunId` then); `reopened` says whether a *resolved* cluster was set back to open |
| `flakiness.spike` | A completed run contains flaky tests; the flakiness-threshold filter keeps only rates above N% |
| `perf.regression` | A run is at least 20% slower than the median of the previous five complete runs on the same branch and environment (runs of the whole suite: no partial, Flake Lab, probe, bisect or reproduction run, and no environment incident); the regression-% filter raises the bar |
| `diagnosis.completed` | A diagnosis of a cluster, or of one of its failures, is stored: Piwi's (requires an [AI provider](/guide/ai-provider)) or one an agent records. A failure in no cluster sends none |
| `auto_heal.pr_opened` | [Auto-heal](/features/auto-heal) opened a pull request; the payload carries `prNumber`, `prUrl`, `branch` and `editCount` |
| `environment.incident` | A completed run is flagged as an [environment incident](/features/environment-incidents); it replaces the run's `run.failed`, `run.failed.default_branch`, `flakiness.spike`, `perf.regression`, `cluster.new` and `bug.looks_fixed` (`run.finished` still fires). The payload carries `rule`, `reason`, `host`, `otherProjects` and `incidentKey`, which is the same for every run of one outage across projects, so a channel receives one message. A subscription filtered on owners does not receive it |
| `test.stuck` | A running test of a live run has run longer than both two minutes and three times its longest duration among its last ten passing executions ([Stuck tests](/features/stuck-tests)), once per attempt; a run started on a developer's machine (origin `local`, `desktop`, `editor`, `preflight` or `bug`) sends none, complete or not, and neither does a run that sends no run event |
| `bug.looks_fixed` | A `test.fail()` test passed in a completed run, in every browser project that ran it, and did not already pass on the previous completed run of the same branch that sends notifications itself; the payload lists the `tests`, each with the bug report (`bugId`, from `piwi:bug`) and ticket (`link`) it names |

**`report.ready`** needs no subscription: a [report schedule](/features/quality-reports#report-schedules) sends it to
the channels it names, through the same outbox. Its webhook body adds the whole report:
`{ "event", "payload": { "snapshotId", "scheduleId", "periodEnd", "url" }, "bundle", "timestamp" }`.

## Webhook body

A webhook channel receives a `POST` with the body `{ "event": "run.failed", "payload": { … }, "timestamp": "…" }`.
For run events the payload includes up to three failing tests, so you can act without a round-trip to the dashboard:

```json
{
  "event": "run.failed",
  "payload": {
    "runId": 42,
    "projectName": "checkout",
    "status": "failed",
    "totalTests": 120,
    "failedTests": 3,
    "passedTests": 114,
    "flakyTests": 2,
    "skippedTests": 3,
    "didNotRunTests": 0,
    "interruptedTests": 0,
    "failingTestCount": 3,
    "branch": "main",
    "environment": "staging",
    "commit": {
      "sha": "3f9c2a1d8e7b6c5d4e3f2a1b0c9d8e7f6a5b4c3d",
      "message": "Validate the card number before enabling Pay",
      "author": "Alex Martin",
      "url": "https://github.com/acme/checkout/commit/3f9c2a1d8e7b6c5d4e3f2a1b0c9d8e7f6a5b4c3d"
    },
    "ciUrl": "https://github.com/acme/checkout/actions/runs/123",
    "origin": "ci",
    "history": [
      { "runId": 40, "status": "passed", "failedTests": 0 },
      { "runId": 41, "status": "passed", "failedTests": 0 },
      { "runId": 42, "status": "failed", "failedTests": 3 }
    ],
    "topFailures": [
      {
        "title": "applies discount code",
        "suitePath": ["Checkout", "Payment"],
        "filePath": "tests/checkout.spec.ts",
        "line": 38,
        "browserName": "chromium",
        "owner": "@acme/payments",
        "headline": "getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay' }) never became enabled, click timed out after 30 s",
        "errorExcerpt": "TimeoutError: locator.click: Timeout 30000ms exceeded.\nlocator resolved to <button disabled>Pay</button>",
        "source": {
          "file": "tests/checkout.spec.ts",
          "line": 42,
          "snippet": "    41 |   await page.getByLabel('Code').fill('SAVE10');\n>   42 |   await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Pay' }).click();\n    43 | });"
        },
        "history": ["passed", "passed", "failed"],
        "testCaseId": 815,
        "executionId": 9001
      }
    ]
  },
  "timestamp": "2026-07-11T10:00:00.000Z"
}
```

`headline` is the one-line explanation the dashboard builds from the Playwright error (the locator, its last state,
the expected and received values, the timeout; see [Failure evidence](/features/evidence#one-execution-diagnosis-first)),
absent when the case carries no error. `errorExcerpt` is the error's message head: at most five lines before the call
log and the stack trace, capped at 300 characters, plus the last `waiting for …` line when the head is only a bare
timeout. Slack and email messages lead with the headline, quote the excerpt and link each failure to its execution.
The [pull-request comment](/features/pr-feedback) quotes failures the same way.

A test is failing when the last attempt of one of its repetitions failed: a test that passed on a retry counts as flaky,
never as a failure. `interruptedTests` counts the tests the run's interruption cut short, in none of the other counts. `topFailures` names the first three, `failingTestCount` counts them all, each test once per
Playwright project however many of its `--repeat-each` repetitions failed (`failedTests` counts each failed repetition),
and `owners` covers every failed attempt, so a team hears of its flaky test's failed first attempt. Each failure names its describe blocks (`suitePath`), the line it is declared on, its Playwright project
(`browserName`) and its `owner`. `source` holds the lines around the line the failure threw at, as the reporter
captured them: the test file, or the helper the error's stack points at, from four lines before it to two after, the
failing line marked `>`.

`origin` is what launched the run: `ci`, `local`, `desktop`, … ([run origin](/reference/test-metadata#run-origin)).

`history` lists the run and up to nine runs before it on the same branch and environment, oldest first: the ended runs
that would send notifications themselves ([which runs send none](/reference/test-metadata#run-origin), an
environment incident included). Each failure's `history` gives that test's outcome in each of those runs (`passed`, `flaky`, `failed`,
`skipped`, `didnotrun` for a test that did not run, `interrupted` for one the run's interruption cut short, in no
outcome, or `null` when the run did not report it). `commit`
comes from the run's Git metadata, linked when the project's repository host is known, and `ciUrl` from its CI
metadata.

## Emails

Every event has its own email. A run's email opens with its outcome in large type, then a bar of its tests by outcome,
its `history` as a row of squares with what it says (_First failure after 6 passing runs_), the commit and the CI
build. Each failure in `topFailures` shows its full name with its describe blocks, its file and line, its `source`
syntax-highlighted with the failing line marked, its error with the expected and received values in color, and its own
`history`, which tells a new failure from one that keeps coming back. A digest lists each event with its run's outcome
bar.

## Slack and Microsoft Teams

A Slack message heads with the email's headline and keeps the rest in an attachment whose side stripe takes the
event's color: the run's tests by outcome and its `history` as rows of colored squares, the commit, the CI build and the
owners as fields, then each failure with its describe blocks, its file and line, its `source` with the failing line
marked, its error and its own `history`, and buttons to the run and the build. A Slack-compatible server (Mattermost,
Rocket.Chat) shows the message's text line, and none of its blocks.

A Microsoft Teams card sets the headline on a band of the event's color and draws the outcomes as a stacked bar chart.
Each failure's code goes in a code block Teams colors by language, and its error's expected and received lines are green
and red. Where a Teams client draws no chart or code block (the mobile app), the card shows the same squares and
numbered lines instead.

## Payload fields by event

Every event that comes from a run carries that run's `branch` and `environment` when the run reported them: the
`run.*` events, `flakiness.spike`, `perf.regression`, the `cluster.*` events, `bug.looks_fixed` and `test.stuck`. When
the run's environment label resolves to one of the project's [environments](/features/environments), the event also
carries its `environmentName`, `environmentKey` and `environmentAliases`. A subscription's
[branch and environment filters](/features/notifications#branches-and-environments) match on these fields.

- **Run events** (`run.*`, `flakiness.spike`, `perf.regression`): the run, its counts, `topFailures`, and the `owners`
  of the failing tests. `perf.regression` adds `durationMs`, `baselineDurationMs` and `regressionPct`.
- **`cluster.new`**: the cluster's `signature` and `title`, `sampleErrorExcerpt` (cut like `errorExcerpt`),
  `affectedCases`, the `owners` of the tests that failed into it in that run, and `firstSeenRunId` when it first
  appeared in an earlier run, which sent no notification of it.
- **`cluster.fixed`** and **`cluster.regressed`**: the cluster's `signature`, `title` and the `runId` that decided the
  verdict; for a fix, the `commit` and `timeToResolutionMs`. With an [SCM credential](/guide/source-control), a `fixAuthor`
  object (`{ name, email }`) names the author of the fixing commit (for a regression, of the fix that did not hold).
  A fix landed by an [auto-heal PR](/features/auto-heal#after-the-pr-opens) carries `healPr` (`{ number, url, actionId }`).
- **`diagnosis.completed`**: the cluster, and the diagnosis's `summary`, `rootCause`, `category` and `confidence`. A
  diagnosis of one failure in the cluster adds its `executionId`, and the notification opens that failure.
- **`test.stuck`**: the run, the test's `testTitle`, `suitePath` and `location`, the `browserName`, `shardIndex` and
  worker it runs in (`parallelIndex`, its lane from 0, which the message shows from 1 as `worker 2`, absent from an
  older reporter; `workerIndex`, Playwright's worker process), the attempt's `startedAt` (epoch ms), `elapsedMs` (how
  long it had run) and `usualMs` (its longest passing duration), and the test's `owners`.

A `cluster.*` event also carries `knownIssue` (`{ key, url }`) when the cluster is linked to a tracker issue.

## Verifying a webhook

When the channel has a secret, each request carries an `X-Piwi-Signature` header, so you can verify that Piwi sent
it. Its value is `sha256=` followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, keyed with the secret:

```
X-Piwi-Signature: sha256=5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592...
```

To check it, compute the HMAC over the exact bytes you received, never a re-serialized payload, and compare the two in
constant time. In Node.js:

```typescript
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from 'node:crypto'

function isFromPiwi(rawBody: Buffer, header: string | undefined, secret: string): boolean {
  const expected = Buffer.from(`sha256=${createHmac('sha256', secret).update(rawBody).digest('hex')}`)
  const received = Buffer.from(header ?? '')
  return received.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(received, expected)
}
```

A channel with no secret sends no header. Webhook secrets are encrypted at rest.
